work: Enarratio in Epistolam I B. Pauli ad Thessalonicenses
source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. XIII (Montreuil)

1.title: ELUCIDATIO CAPITULI PRIMI : PAULUS ET SILVANUS ET TIMOTHEUS.
1.title_en: Explanation of the first chapter: Paul and Sylvanus and Timothy.

paras.t: Paulus et Silvanus et Timotheus mandant Ecclesiæ Thessalonicensium, id est fidelibus in Thessalonica congregatis, et per fidem atque dilectionem unitis, in Deo Patre nostro et Domino nostro Jesu Christo, id est ad gloriam Patris et Christi Filii ejus, vel secundum voluntatem Dei Patris et Christi. Non apponit nomen gloriæ suæ, dicendo, Paulus apostolus, quoniam Thessalonicenses nihil indignum de ipso senserunt. Unde non eguerunt de excellentia ejus amplius informari. Silvanus autem iste, quem sibi adjungit Apostolus, secundum Haymonem et alios quosdam, est Silas, de quo in Actibus multa magnifica recitantur. Nam tantæ perfectionis extiterat, ut unus de primis seu summis fratribus primitivæ Ecclesiæ in Jerusalem congregatæ, et propheta fuisse scribitur a Luca. Sed et apostolus appellatur. Et quoniam Silvanus ac Timotheus cooperati fuerunt Apostolo in Thessalonicensium conversione, idcirco eos sibi in salutatione annectit. Solus tamen Paulus dictavit epistolam, imo Spiritus Sanctus per eum. Gratia vobis et pax divinitus infundatur, conservetur et perficiatur.
paras.en: [[1:1|Paul and Sylvanus and Timothy|Paulus et Silvanus et Timotheus]] send greeting [[1:1|to the church of the Thessalonians|Ecclesiæ Thessalonicensium]], that is, to the faithful gathered together in Thessalonica and united by faith and love, [[1:1|in God the Father and in the Lord Jesus Christ|in Deo Patre nostro et Domino nostro Jesu Christo]]: that is, to the glory of the Father and of Christ his Son, or according to the will of God the Father and of Christ. He does not add the title of his dignity by saying "Paul, an apostle," since the Thessalonians had thought nothing unworthy of him; so they had no need to be further informed of his eminence. This Sylvanus whom the Apostle joins to himself is, according to Haymo and certain others, Silas, of whom many great things are told in the Acts[[Acts 15:22||]] [the margin gives Acts xv–xvii, where Silas appears throughout]. For he was of such perfection that Luke writes that he was one of the first or chief brethren of the primitive Church gathered in Jerusalem[[Acts 15:22||]], and a prophet[[Acts 15:32||]] [the margin's verse here is unread; Acts 15:32 is the verse that calls him a prophet]. He is also called an apostle. And since Sylvanus and Timothy worked with the Apostle in the conversion of the Thessalonians, he therefore joins them with himself in the greeting. Yet Paul alone dictated the epistle; or rather the Holy Ghost through him. [[1:2|Grace be to you and peace|Gratia vobis et pax]]: may they be poured into you from God, kept and made perfect.

paras.t: Narrationem insuper orditur Apostolus a gratiarum actione. Gratias agimus Deo, ex caritate divina atque fraterna, qua Dei honorem optamus, et vestro profectui congaudemus, semper, id est omni hora convenienti, pro omnibus vobis, id est vice vestri, vel de vobis, videlicet pro beneficiis Dei vobis collatis; memoriam vestri facientes in orationibus nostris, quas Deo sine intermissione offerimus, id est omni tempore opportuno; memores operis fidei vestræ, id est laudabilis conversationis ex fide nascentis (vel, opus fidei vocatur oris confessio), et laboris, quem in cultu divino habuistis, et caritatis, id est actualis dilectionis vestræ in Deum et proximum, et sustinentiæ spei, id est tolerantiæ adversitatum, quæ procedit ex spe Domini nostri Jesu Christi, id est ex spe futuræ beatitudinis: quam spem Christus ut Deus, creando imprimit nobis. Consideratio enim præmii minuit vim flagelli. Sic ergo memoriam vestri facimus ante Deum et Patrem vestrum, id est in conspectu sanctæ Trinitatis, quam et pro vestro profectu jugiter imploramus.
paras.en: Further, the Apostle begins his narration with thanksgiving. [[1:2|We give thanks to God|Gratias agimus Deo]], out of divine and brotherly charity, by which we desire the honour of God and rejoice together in your progress, [[1:2|always|semper]], that is, at every fitting hour, [[1:2|for you all|pro omnibus vobis]], that is, on your behalf, or concerning you, namely for the benefits God has bestowed on you; [[1:2|making a remembrance of you in our prayers|memoriam vestri facientes in orationibus nostris]], which we offer to God [[1:2|without ceasing|sine intermissione]], that is, at every suitable time; [[1:3|Being mindful of the work of your faith|memores operis fidei vestræ]], that is, of the praiseworthy manner of life that springs from faith (or, the work of faith is the name for the confession of the mouth), [[1:3|and labour|et laboris]], which you have had in the worship of God, [[1:3|and charity|et caritatis]], that is, of your love in act towards God and your neighbour, [[1:3|and of the enduring of the hope|et sustinentiæ spei]], that is, of the bearing of adversities, which proceeds from the hope [[1:3|of our Lord Jesus Christ|Domini nostri Jesu Christi]], that is, from the hope of the bliss to come: which hope Christ, as God, impresses upon us by creating it. For the thought of the reward lessens the force of the scourge. So then we make remembrance of you [[1:3|before God and our Father|ante Deum et Patrem vestrum]] [Denis reads "your Father"], that is, in the sight of the Holy Trinity, which we also implore continually for your progress.

paras.t: Scientes, id est, nos qui vobis hæc scribimus, agnoscentes, o fratres dilecti a Deo: conjective, inquam, vel certo scientes ex revelatione, electionem vestram, id est prædestinationem, videlicet quod præordinati estis ad vitam æternam; vel, vos, o fratres dilecti, eam scientes per quædam signa prædestinationis: de quibus subjungitur: quia evangelium nostrum, id est evangelica prædicatio, non fuit ad vos in sermone tantum, id est, non nudis verbis firmata est, sed et in virtute miraculorum, id est per miracula roborabatur, et Spiritu Sancto, id est, per manifesta dona Spiritus Sancti prædicatio nostra fulta est, et in plenitudine multa, id est, in magna abundantia divinorum charismatum prædicavimus vobis. Per impositionem namque manuum mearum datus est vobis Spiritus Sanctus in Baptismo, etiam in signo visibili. Simile huic est quod ad Hebræos dicit Apostolus: Quomodo effugiemus, si tantam neglexerimus salutem, quæ in nos confirmata est, contestante Deo signis et portentis et variis virtutibus, et Spiritus Sancti distributionibus? Unde apud Marcum legimus: Illi profecti prædicaverunt ubique, Domino cooperante et sermonem confirmante sequentibus signis. Unde per hæc magna miracula Thessalonicenses facile crediderunt. Sicut scitis per experientiam, quæ est magistra veritatis, quales fuerimus verbo et opere, in vobis, id est inter vos, et hoc, propter vos, id est propter vestram conversionem atque salutem.
paras.en: [[1:4|Knowing|Scientes]]: that is, we who write these things to you, recognising, O [[1:4|brethren, beloved of God|fratres dilecti a Deo]]; knowing, I say, by conjecture, or knowing for certain by revelation, [[1:4|your election|electionem vestram]], that is, your predestination, namely that you have been foreordained to eternal life; or, you, O beloved brethren, knowing it by certain signs of predestination, of which he adds: [[1:5|For our gospel|quia evangelium nostrum]], that is, the preaching of the gospel, [[1:5|hath not been unto you in word only|non fuit ad vos in sermone tantum]], that is, was not confirmed by bare words, [[1:5|but in power also|sed et in virtute]] of miracles, that is, it was strengthened by miracles, [[1:5|and in the Holy Ghost|et Spiritu Sancto]], that is, our preaching was upheld by manifest gifts of the Holy Ghost, [[1:5|and in much fulness|et in plenitudine multa]], that is, we preached to you in great abundance of divine gifts [Latin *charismata*, the graces freely given, such as tongues and miracles]. For through the laying on of my hands the Holy Ghost was given to you in Baptism, and with a visible sign as well. Like this is what the Apostle says to the Hebrews: [[Heb 2:3|How shall we escape if we neglect so great salvation?|Quomodo effugiemus, si tantam neglexerimus salutem]]? which [[Heb 2:3|was confirmed unto us|in nos confirmata est]], [[Heb 2:4|God also bearing them witness by signs and wonders and divers miracles and distributions of the Holy Ghost|contestante Deo signis et portentis et variis virtutibus, et Spiritus Sancti distributionibus?]]? Hence we read in Mark: [[Mark 16:20|they going forth preached every where: the Lord working withal, and confirming the word with signs that followed|Illi profecti prædicaverunt ubique, Domino cooperante et sermonem confirmante sequentibus signis]]. So through these great miracles the Thessalonians readily believed. [[1:5|as you know|Sicut scitis]] by experience, which is the teacher of truth, [[1:5|what manner of men we have been|quales fuerimus]] in word and deed [[1:5|among you|in vobis]], that is, in your midst, and this [[1:5|for your sakes|propter vos]], that is, for your conversion and salvation.

paras.t: Et vos, o fratres, imitatores nostri facti estis, id est, nostra vestigia estis secuti, multa adversa propter justitiam patiendo, et Domini, id est, etiam Christum imitati estis, conformando vos passionibus ejus: quia ut ille a populo suo dura perpessus est, ita et vos a civibus vestris; excipientes verbum, id est prædicationi nostræ consentientes, in tribulatione multa, id est cum magna persecutione vobis a perversis illata propter fidei receptionem. Excipientes, inquam, cum gaudio Spiritus Sancti, id est cum interna consolatione a Spiritu Sancto infusa, ita quod licet exterius tribularemini, intus tamen a Spiritu Sancto lætificabamini: prout Apostolus idem alibi ait, Sicut abundant passiones Christi in nobis, ita et per Christum abundat consolatio nostra. Ita ut facti sitis forma, id est perfectionis fideique exemplar imitatione dignissimum, omnibus credentibus in Macedonia et in Achaia, quæ sunt provinciæ Græciæ.
paras.en: [[1:6|And you|Et vos]], O brethren, [[1:6|became followers of us|imitatores nostri facti estis]], that is, you have followed in our footsteps, suffering many adversities for justice' sake, [[1:6|and of the Lord|et Domini]], that is, you have imitated Christ as well, conforming yourselves to his sufferings: for as he suffered hard things from his own people, so have you from your fellow citizens; [[1:6|receiving the word|excipientes verbum]], that is, consenting to our preaching, [[1:6|in much tribulation|in tribulatione multa]], that is, with great persecution brought upon you by the wicked for receiving the faith. Receiving it, I say, [[1:6|with joy of the Holy Ghost|cum gaudio Spiritus Sancti]], that is, with inward consolation poured in by the Holy Ghost, so that though you were troubled outwardly, yet inwardly you were gladdened by the Holy Ghost: as the same Apostle says elsewhere, [[2 Cor 1:5|as the sufferings of Christ abound in us: so also by Christ doth our comfort abound|Sicut abundant passiones Christi in nobis, ita et per Christum abundat consolatio nostra]]. [[1:7|So that you were made a pattern|Ita ut facti sitis forma]], that is, an example of perfection and of faith most worthy of imitation, [[1:7|to all that believe in Macedonia and in Achaia|omnibus credentibus in Macedonia et in Achaia]], which are provinces of Greece.

paras.t: A vobis enim diffamatus, id est divulgatus, est materialiter sermo Domini: id est, a vobis propter perfectionem vestram, sumpserunt alii occasionem loquendi, laudandi ac prædicandi verbum Dei, tanquam accensi vestro exemplo. Et non solum in Macedonia et in Achaia, sed et in omni loco Christianorum ad quos fama vestra pervenit, fides vestra quæ est ad Deum, id est, qua ipsi in Deum tenditis, perfecta est, id est, plena et inclyta reputatur, ita ut non sit nobis necesse quidquam loqui de ampliori præconio vestri, vel pro informatione vestri, vel de vobis ad alios incitandos.
paras.en: [[1:8|For from you was spread abroad|A vobis enim diffamatus]], that is, made known, materially [that is, they were the matter and occasion of its spreading, not its preachers], [[1:8|the word of the Lord|sermo Domini]]: that is, from you, because of your perfection, others took occasion to speak of, praise and preach the word of God, as though fired by your example. And [[1:8|not only in Macedonia and in Achaia|non solum in Macedonia et in Achaia]], [[1:8|but also in every place|sed et in omni loco]] of Christians to whom your fame has come, [[1:8|your faith which is towards God|fides vestra quæ est ad Deum]], that is, by which you yourselves tend towards God, is perfect [Denis reads *perfecta est*, "is perfect", where the Vulgate has *profecta est*, "is gone forth"], that is, is reckoned full and renowned, [[1:8|so that we need not to speak any thing|ita ut non sit nobis necesse quidquam loqui]] in further praise of you, or for your instruction, or about you in order to stir others on.

paras.t: Ipsi enim quibus nota est fides et conversatio vestra, de vobis annuntiant, id est, ad laudem vestri testantur, qualem introitum habuerimus ad vos, id est, quam fructuosus, felix et expeditus fuit ingressus noster ad vos, quorum tantam multitudinem tam perfecte convertimus, et quomodo, id est quam perfecte, conversi estis ad Deum a simulacris, id est idololatriam deserendo, servire, id est ad serviendum, Deo vivo et vero: per quem hoc loco intelligitur persona Patris, nam subditur: et exspectare quotidie, ut sitis semper parati ad mortem, Filium ejus venturum de cœlis manifeste in die judicii: qui quotidie exspectandus est, ut simus jugiter præparati visitari ab eo per mortem, prout ipse apud Lucam loquitur: Et vos similes hominibus exspectantibus dominum suum quando revertatur a nuptiis; et denuo alibi, Estote parati, quia qua hora non putatis, Filius hominis veniet. Quem Pater suscitavit ex mortuis tertia die, videlicet Jesum, qui sua passione eripuit nos ab ira ventura, id est a pœna æterna seu damnationis sententia, quæ in die judicii contra impios proferetur. Nunc enim eripuit nos, quantum in ipso est, a peccatis propter quæ ira illa infligitur.
paras.en: [[1:9|For they themselves|Ipsi enim]], to whom your faith and manner of life are known, [[1:9|relate|annuntiant]] of you [Denis reads *de vobis*, "of you", where the Vulgate has *de nobis*, "of us"], that is, bear witness to your praise, [[1:9|what manner of entering in we had unto you|qualem introitum habuerimus ad vos]], that is, how fruitful, happy and unhindered was our coming in among you, so great a multitude of whom we converted so perfectly, [[1:9|and how|et quomodo]], that is, how perfectly, [[1:9|you turned to God from idols|conversi estis ad Deum a simulacris]], that is, by forsaking idolatry, [[1:9|to serve|servire]], that is, in order to serve [[1:9|the living and true God|Deo vivo et vero]]: by whom in this place the person of the Father is meant, for it follows: [[1:10|And to wait for|et exspectare]] daily, so that you may be always ready for death, [[1:10|his Son|Filium ejus]], who is to come [[1:10|from heaven|de cœlis]] openly on the day of judgment: who is to be awaited daily, so that we may be ever prepared to be visited by him through death, as he himself says in Luke: [[Luke 12:36|And you yourselves like to men who wait for their lord, when he shall return from the wedding|Et vos similes hominibus exspectantibus dominum suum quando revertatur a nuptiis]]; and again elsewhere, [[Luke 12:40|Be you then also ready: for at what hour you think not the Son of man will come|Estote parati, quia qua hora non putatis, Filius hominis veniet]] [the margin gives "Ibid. 40"; Denis's "elsewhere" is in fact the same chapter]. [[1:10|whom he raised up from the dead|Quem Pater suscitavit ex mortuis]], that is, the Father, on the third day, namely [[1:10|Jesus, who|Jesum, qui]] by his passion [[1:10|hath delivered us from the wrath to come|eripuit nos ab ira ventura]], that is, from eternal punishment, or the sentence of damnation, which will be pronounced against the wicked on the day of judgment. For he has delivered us now, as far as lies in him, from the sins for which that wrath is inflicted.

2.title: EXPOSITIO CAPITULI SECUNDI : NAM ET IPSI SCITIS, FRATRES, ETC.
2.title_en: Exposition of the second chapter: For yourselves know, brethren, etc.

paras.t: In superiori capitulo gratias egit Apostolus Deo pro beneficiis Thessalonicensibus impertitis, bona quoque Thessalonicensium commendavit; nunc suæ prædicationis veritatem ostendit ex sinceritate conversationis quam habuit inter Thessalonicenses.
paras.en: In the preceding chapter the Apostle gave thanks to God for the benefits bestowed on the Thessalonians, and also commended the good things of the Thessalonians; now he shows the truth of his preaching from the sincerity of the life he led among the Thessalonians.

paras.t: Quemadmodum enim, secundum philosophos, operatio arguit formam, sic conversatio monstrat legis ac fidei qualitatem. Nam et unumquodque judicandum est secundum maximum in quod potest, juxta Philosophum. Lex igitur christiana judicanda est secundum suum principale, finale ac summum, ad quod suum observatorem perducit. Hoc autem est privati amoris plena exstinctio, atque divini amoris pura ardensque affectio. Ad quam perfectionem perducit lex Christi per ordinatissima atque honestissima media: quæ sunt evangelica consilia ac præcepta, quibus humilitas, patientia, paupertas, castitas, mansuetudo, obedientia, similesque virtutes jubentur aut consulantur. Omnis vero carnalitas, falsitas, simulatio, dæmonum pactio, prohibitarum artium usus, penitus condemnatur et exstirpatur ab ea. Quæ omnia tanto certius innotescent hominibus, quanto evangelicam legem custodierint plenius. Unde internis ac devotissimis famulis Christi, ipsa fides christianæque legis munditia, quasi experientia constat quia vere a Deo fluxerunt. Propter quod ait Salvator: Si quis voluerit voluntatem Dei facere, cognoscet de doctrina utrum ex Deo sit, an ego a me ipso loquar. Nec ignoramus quanta faciat Deus pro his qui evangelicam legem perfecte custodiunt, quanta pro eis agat miracula, quomodo eos in vita, in morte, et post mortem mirifice, quam ineffabiliter eos vicissim consoletur, accendat, deificet, rapiat atque absorbeat. Quod qui experitur, de nullo adeo certus est sicut de fidei veritate christianæque legis sanctitate.
paras.en: For as, according to the philosophers, the operation shows the form, so the manner of life shows the quality of a law and of a faith. For each thing is to be judged by the utmost of which it is capable, according to the Philosopher. The Christian law, then, is to be judged by its principal, final and highest end, to which it leads him who keeps it. And this is the full extinction of private love [that is, of self-love], and the pure and burning affection of divine love. To this perfection the law of Christ leads by the most ordered and most honourable means: these are the evangelical counsels and precepts, by which humility, patience, poverty, chastity, meekness, obedience and the like virtues are commanded or counselled. But all carnality, falsehood, pretence, pacts with demons, and the use of forbidden arts are utterly condemned and rooted out by it. All these things will become known to men the more surely, the more fully they have kept the law of the Gospel. Hence to the inward and most devout servants of Christ it is plain, as it were by experience, that the faith itself and the purity of the Christian law truly flowed from God. Wherefore the Saviour says: [[John 7:17|If any man will do the will of|Si quis voluerit voluntatem]] God, [[John 7:17|he shall know of the doctrine, whether it be of God, or whether I speak of myself|cognoscet de doctrina utrum ex Deo sit, an ego a me ipso loquar]]. Nor are we ignorant how much God does for those who keep the law of the Gospel perfectly, how many miracles he works for them, how wonderfully he deals with them in life, in death and after death, how unspeakably he in turn consoles, kindles, deifies, ravishes and absorbs them. He who experiences this is certain of nothing so much as of the truth of the faith and the holiness of the Christian law.

paras.t: Effectum vero redemptionis istius per sacramenta consequimur; et tandem ab omni pœnalitate et imperfectione carnis ac animæ, merito dominicæ passionis eripiemur, quando mortale hoc induet immortalitatem.
paras.en: [This sentence stands in the transcription in the middle of the word *Propter* (“Pro-” … “-pter quod”), breaking the sentence above; it seems to belong elsewhere and is kept here as printed.] And we obtain the effect of this redemption through the sacraments; and at last we shall be delivered from all penalty and imperfection of flesh and soul, by the merit of the Lord's passion, when [[1 Cor 15:54|this mortal hath put on immortality|mortale hoc induet immortalitatem]].

paras.t: Ait ergo beatus Apostolus: Nam et ipsi scitis, fratres, id est, ideo dixi prædicta, videlicet quod alii annuntiant qualem introitum habuerimus ad vos, nam et vos ipsi, o fratres, scitis introitum nostrum, id est qualitatem adventus nostri, ad vos convertendos, quia non inanis fuit, id est non infructuosus, non levis, non sine debito fine; sed ante accessum istum ad vos, passi diversa tormenta, et contumeliis affecti, sicut scitis aliorum relatu vel proprio visu, in Philippis, urbe Macedoniæ vobis propinqua atque subjecta. Ibi enim Paulus et Silas virgis cæsi et incarcerati, imo durissime vincti fuerunt, occasione puellæ quam Paulus a spiritu pythonico liberavit. Fiduciam habuimus in Deo nostro, innitendo ejus auxilio, non propriis viribus, loqui, id est ad non inaniter loquendum, ad vos Evangelium Dei in multa sollicitudine, id est cum ingenti cura ac diligentia.
paras.en: The blessed Apostle therefore says: [[2:1|For yourselves know, brethren|Nam et ipsi scitis, fratres]]: that is, I said the foregoing, namely that others tell what manner of entrance we had to you, for you yourselves too, O brethren, know [[2:1|our entrance|introitum nostrum]], that is, the manner of our coming, [[2:1|in unto you|ad vos]] to convert you, [[2:1|that it was not in vain|quia non inanis fuit]], that is, not fruitless, not light, not without its due end; [[2:2|But having suffered many things before|sed ante accessum istum ad vos, passi diversa tormenta]] [Denis expands: “before this coming to you, having suffered divers torments”], [[2:2|and been shamefully treated, (as you know)|et contumeliis affecti, sicut scitis]] by others' report or by your own sight, [[2:2|at Philippi|in Philippis]], a city of Macedonia near you and subject to it. For there Paul and Silas were beaten with rods and imprisoned, indeed most harshly bound, on account of the girl whom Paul delivered from the spirit of divination[[Acts 16:12||]] [the margin gives Acts xvi, 12 and following; the scourging and prison are at Acts 16:22–24]. [[2:2|we had confidence in our God|Fiduciam habuimus in Deo nostro]], relying on his help, not on our own strength, [[2:2|to speak|loqui]], that is, so as to speak not in vain, [[2:2|unto you the gospel of God in much carefulness|ad vos Evangelium Dei in multa sollicitudine]], that is, with great care and diligence.

paras.t: Exhortatio enim nostra, id est prædicatio qua admonuimus vos, processit non de errore, id est ex interiori falsitate aut infidelitate, sicut exhortatio hæreticorum, neque de immunditia, id est ex lascivo affectu aut prava intentione; neque in dolo vobis proposita est: quia ut beatus Job loquitur, non indiget Deus nostro mendacio, ut pro illo dolos loquamur. Sed sicut probati, id est approbati vel electi, sumus a Deo, ut crederetur nobis Evangelium, id est, prædicatio evangelicæ legis nobis committeretur, ita loquimur, sicut divinitus instituti sumus, non quasi hominibus placentes, id est finaliter placere quærentes, quoniam Deus dissipavit ossa eorum qui hominibus placent, sed Deo qui probat, id est per prospera et adversa examinat, tentat et approbat, corda nostra, aliisque probata ostendit: juxta illud Sapientiæ, Tanquam aurum in fornace probavit electos Dominus, et quasi holocausti hostiam accepit illos.
paras.en: [[2:3|For our exhortation|Exhortatio enim nostra]], that is, the preaching with which we admonished you, came [[2:3|not of error|non de errore]], that is, from inward falsehood or unbelief, as the exhortation of heretics does, [[2:3|nor of uncleanness|neque de immunditia]], that is, from wanton affection or a wicked intention; [[2:3|nor in deceit|neque in dolo]] was it set before you: for, as blessed Job says, God has no need [[Job 13:7|of your lie, that you should speak deceitfully for him|nostro mendacio, ut pro illo dolos loquamur]] [Denis: “of our lie, that we should speak deceitfully”]. [[2:4|But as we were approved|Sed sicut probati]], that is, found worthy or chosen, [[2:4|by God that the gospel should be committed to us|sumus a Deo, ut crederetur nobis Evangelium]], that is, that the preaching of the law of the Gospel should be entrusted to us, [[2:4|even so we speak|ita loquimur]], as we have been taught from God, [[2:4|not as pleasing men|non quasi hominibus placentes]], that is, not seeking to please them as our end, since [[Ps 52:6|God hath scattered the bones of them that please men|Deus dissipavit ossa eorum qui hominibus placent]], [[2:4|but God, who proveth|sed Deo qui probat]], that is, examines, tries and approves through prosperity and adversity, [[2:4|our hearts|corda nostra]], and shows them, once proved, to others: according to that word of Wisdom, [[Wis 3:6|As gold in the furnace|Tanquam aurum in fornace]] the Lord hath proved his elect, [[Wis 3:6|and as a victim of a holocaust, he hath received them|et quasi holocausti hostiam accepit illos]].

paras.t: Neque enim aliquando fuimus in sermone adulationis, id est, nunquam vobis adulanter locuti sumus, sicut scitis. Unde in Proverbiis Salomon docet: Non lactes quemquam labiis tuis; et Psalmographus, Oleum peccatoris non impinguet caput meum. Neque in occasione avaritiæ, id est, temporale commodum nec directe nec indirecte quæsivimus. Deus testis est, qui apud Jeremiam dicit: Ego sum judex et testis.
paras.en: [[2:5|For neither have we used at any time the speech of flattery|Neque enim aliquando fuimus in sermone adulationis]], that is, we never spoke to you flatteringly, [[2:5|as you know|sicut scitis]]. Hence Solomon teaches in Proverbs: [[Prov 24:28|deceive not any man with thy lips|Non lactes quemquam labiis tuis]] [*lactes*, literally “suckle,” that is, coax or flatter; the margin gives Prov. xxiv, 26, but the words are at Prov 24:28]; and the Psalmist: [[Ps 140:5|let not the oil of the sinner fatten my head|Oleum peccatoris non impinguet caput meum]]. [[2:5|nor taken an occasion of covetousness|Neque in occasione avaritiæ]], that is, we sought no temporal profit, neither directly nor indirectly. [[2:5|God is witness|Deus testis est]], who says in Jeremias: [[Jer 29:23|I am the judge and the witness|Ego sum judex et testis]].

paras.t: Nec quærentes ab hominibus gloriam, id est laudem, famæ clarificationem, aut venerationem, videlicet neque a vobis, neque ab aliis: quum, id est licet, possemus vobis oneri esse, id est debitam, imo et magnam venerationem a vobis exigere, ut Christi apostoli, id est in quantum summi Sacerdotis vicarii: non tamen referendo honorem ad nos, sed ad Christum finaliter. Vel sic: Quum possemus vobis oneri esse, id est gravamen quoddam vobis inducere, requirendo a vobis stipendia vitæ, ut Christi apostoli, qui spiritualia seminando, merentur vestra temporalia metere, id est de vestris temporalibus sustentari ac vivere. Sed facti sumus parvuli, id est humiles, in medio vestrum, exemplo Christi dicentis: Ego in medio vestrum sum sicut qui ministrat; tanquam si nutrix foveat filios suos proprio lacte in gremio suo.
paras.en: [[2:6|Nor sought we glory of men|Nec quærentes ab hominibus gloriam]], that is, praise, the brightness of fame, or veneration, namely [[2:6|neither of you, nor of others|neque a vobis, neque ab aliis]]: [[2:7|Whereas|quum]], that is, although, [[2:7|we might have been burdensome to you|possemus vobis oneri esse]], that is, might have required of you due, nay great, veneration, [[2:7|as the apostles of Christ|ut Christi apostoli]], that is, inasmuch as we are vicars of the High Priest; yet not referring the honour to ourselves, but to Christ as its end. Or thus: [[2:7|Whereas we might have been burdensome to you|Quum possemus vobis oneri esse]], that is, might have laid a certain burden on you, by asking of you the wages of our living, [[2:7|as the apostles of Christ|ut Christi apostoli]], who by sowing spiritual things deserve to reap your temporal things[[1 Cor 9:11||]], that is, to be supported and to live by your temporal goods. [[2:7|but we became little ones|Sed facti sumus parvuli]], that is, humble, [[2:7|in the midst of you|in medio vestrum]], after the example of Christ, who says: [[Luke 22:27|I am in the midst of you, as he that serveth|Ego in medio vestrum sum sicut qui ministrat]]; [[2:7|as if a nurse should cherish her children|tanquam si nutrix foveat filios suos]] with her own milk in her lap.

paras.t: Ita, id est tam affectuose, pie atque sollicite, desiderantes vos cupide, id est, non bona vestra exteriora, aut temporalia emolimenta optantes ferventer, sed vestram salutem, volebamus tradere vobis non solum Evangelium Dei, sed etiam animas nostras, id est nos ipsos vel vitam nostram, quasi parati mori, pro vestro profectu et vestro obsequio nos exponentes, quoniam carissimi nobis facti estis, fidem recipiendo, tenendo, et optime conservando. Ex iis liquet, bonum ac licitum esse, interdum aliis demonstrare dilectionis affectum qui ad ipsos habetur. Hoc tamen interdum per accidens malum est, videlicet quoniam habet speciem adulationis, vel quoniam generat alteri gloriam vanam.
paras.en: [[2:8|So|Ita]], that is, so affectionately, tenderly and carefully, [[2:8|desirous of you|desiderantes vos]] [[2:8|gladly|cupide]], that is, ardently longing not for your outward goods or temporal gains [the edition prints *emolimenta* for *emolumenta*, “gains”], but for your salvation, [[2:8|we would|volebamus]] [[2:8|impart unto you not only the gospel of God but also our own souls|tradere vobis non solum Evangelium Dei, sed etiam animas nostras]], that is, ourselves or our life, as men ready to die, exposing ourselves for your progress and your service, [[2:8|because you were become most dear unto us|quoniam carissimi nobis facti estis]], by receiving the faith, holding it and keeping it excellently. From this it is clear that it is good and lawful sometimes to show others the affection of love one has for them. Yet this is sometimes bad by accident, namely because it has the appearance of flattery, or because it breeds vainglory in the other.

paras.t: Denique veritatem horum probat Apostolus, per agnitionem eorum quibus hæc mandat. Memores enim estis, fratres, laboris nostri et fatigationis, non solum in prædicando, et cetera divini cultus officia prosequendo, sed etiam manualiter laborando. Nocte ac die laborantes manibus nostris pro necessariis vitæ, ne quem, id est aliquem, vestrum gravaremus, vivendo de sumptibus vestris, prædicavimus in vobis, id est inter vos, Evangelium Dei.
paras.en: Lastly the Apostle proves the truth of these things by the knowledge of those to whom he writes them. [[2:9|For you remember, brethren, our labour and toil|Memores enim estis, fratres, laboris nostri et fatigationis]], not only in preaching and in carrying out the other offices of divine worship, but also in labouring with our hands. [[2:9|working night and day|Nocte ac die laborantes]] [Denis reads *laborantes*, “labouring,” where the Vulgate has *operantes*; the transcription notes *operantes*] with our hands for the necessities of life, [[2:9|lest we should be chargeable to any of you|ne quem, id est aliquem, vestrum gravaremus]] by living at your cost, [[2:9|we preached among you|prædicavimus in vobis]], that is, in your midst, [[2:9|the gospel of God|Evangelium Dei]].

paras.t: Vos enim testes estis, et Deus: de quo in Job dicitur, Ecce in cœlo est testis meus, et conscius meus in excelsis: quam sancte, et juste, et sine querela, id est sine offensa ac reprehensione, vobis qui credidistis, fuimus, conversando inter vos multum juste, sancte atque perfecte;
paras.en: [[2:10|You are witnesses, and God also|Vos enim testes estis, et Deus]], of whom it is said in Job: [[Job 16:20|behold my witness is in heaven, and he that knoweth my conscience is on high|Ecce in cœlo est testis meus, et conscius meus in excelsis]]: [[2:10|how holily and justly and without blame|quam sancte, et juste, et sine querela]], that is, without offence or reproach, [[2:10|we have been to you that have believed|vobis qui credidistis, fuimus]], living among you most justly, holily and perfectly;

paras.t: sicut scitis, qualiter unumquemque vestrum sigillatim, vel omnes cum particulari descensione. (Tanquam pater filios suos […]) precantes vos et consolantes, id est, tam caritative ac diligenter deprecantes vos ad faciendum quæ bona sunt, et consolantes vos contra adversa, sicut pater proprios filios consolatur et instruit. Testificati sumus, id est, cum allegatione testimoniorum sacræ Scripturæ admonuimus, vel sub testimonio Sanctorum adjuravimus, ut ambularetis, id est, de virtute in virtutem procederetis, digne Deo, id est tam reverenter ut decet summo Deo servire, et ut digni sitis beatificari ab eo, qui vocavit vos, per suam inspirationem internam et nostram prædicationem, in suum regnum, id est ad militantis Ecclesiæ (quam Deus nunc regit) societatem, vel, in regnum suum cœleste, ad quod jam vocati estis, et gloriam, id est ad beatitudinem sempiternam.
paras.en: [[2:11|As you know in what manner|sicut scitis, qualiter]] [[2:12|every one of you|unumquemque vestrum]], one by one, or all of you with a coming down to each in particular. [[2:11|(as a father doth his children)|Tanquam pater filios suos]] […] [[2:11|entreating and comforting you|precantes vos et consolantes]] [in the Vulgate these words begin v. 12], that is, so lovingly and diligently entreating you to do what is good, and comforting you against adversity, as a father comforts and instructs his own children. [[2:12|We testified|Testificati sumus]], that is, we admonished you, bringing forward the testimonies of holy Scripture, or adjured you under the witness of the Saints, [[2:12|that you would walk|ut ambularetis]], that is, go on from virtue to virtue, [[2:12|worthy of God|digne Deo]], that is, as reverently as it befits to serve the most high God, and so that you may be worthy to be made blessed by him, [[2:12|who hath called you|qui vocavit vos]] by his inward inspiration and our preaching, [[2:12|unto his kingdom|in suum regnum]], that is, to the fellowship of the Church militant (which God now rules), or into his heavenly kingdom, to which you are now called, [[2:12|and glory|et gloriam]], that is, to everlasting beatitude.

paras.t: Ideo et nos gratias agimus Deo, propter beneficia vobis collata, sine intermissione, id est omni tempore apto; quoniam quum accepissetis a nobis verbum auditus Dei, id est evangelicam prædicationem, quam nos a Deo audivimus atque didicimus: de quo verbo scriptum est in Isaia: Domine, quis credidit auditui nostro, id est verbis quæ a te audivimus? accepistis illud, non ut verbum hominum, id est non cum mediocri attentione, vel consueta hominibus reverentia, sed sicut est vere, verbum Dei, id est cum summa devotione et pleno affectu. Si enim Christus de sua prædicatione testatur, Mea doctrina non est mea, sed ejus qui misit me: multo magis Apostoli dicere potuerunt, Nostrum verbum non est nostrum aut humanum, sed Dei atque divinum. Qui Deus operatur in vobis qui credidistis, id est in vobis credentibus. Operatur autem, non solum præstando habitum gratiæ et virtutum, sed etiam intus movendo et excitando ad bonum.
paras.en: [[2:13|Therefore, we also give thanks to God|Ideo et nos gratias agimus Deo]], for the benefits bestowed on you, [[2:13|without ceasing|sine intermissione]], that is, at every fitting time; [[2:13|because, that when you had received of us the word of the hearing of God|quoniam quum accepissetis a nobis verbum auditus Dei]], that is, the preaching of the Gospel, which we heard and learned from God: of which word it is written in Isaias: Lord, who [[Is 53:1|hath believed our report|quis credidit auditui nostro]] [*auditui*, literally “our hearing,” the same word as *auditus* here], that is, the words which we have heard from thee? [[2:13|you received it not as the word of men|accepistis illud, non ut verbum hominum]], that is, not with middling attention, or with the reverence usual among men, [[2:13|but (as it is indeed) the word of God|sed sicut est vere, verbum Dei]], that is, with the greatest devotion and full affection. For if Christ testifies of his own preaching, [[John 7:16|My doctrine is not mine, but his that sent me|Mea doctrina non est mea, sed ejus qui misit me]] [the margin gives John vii, 10]: much more could the Apostles say, Our word is not ours or human, but God's and divine. [[2:13|who worketh in you that have believed|Qui Deus operatur in vobis qui credidistis]], that is, in you who believe. And he works not only by granting the habit of grace and of the virtues, but also by moving and stirring you inwardly to good.

paras.t: Insuper laudat patientiam atque constantiam Thessalonicensium. Vos enim imitatores facti estis, fratres, Ecclesiarum Dei quæ sunt in Judæa, id est Christifidelium Judæorum, qui in Christo Jesu fundati sunt. Primitiva enim Ecclesia in Judæa collecta, perfectissimæ conversationis fuit: ideo aliarum Ecclesiarum erat exemplar seu forma vivendi. In quo autem illas imitati sunt, adjicit: quia eadem in specie, id est similia mala, passi estis et vos a contribulibus, id est concivibus vestris, sicut et ipsi a Judæis infidelibus, id est qualia fideles Judæi a Judæis infidelibus. Quemadmodum enim legitur in Actibus, Stephano occiso, facta est persecutio magna in Ecclesia Jerosolymitana, et infideles Judæi rapuerunt bona fidelium. De qua persecutione ad Hebræos scribitur: Rememoramini autem pristinos dies, in quibus magnum sustinuistis certamen passionum: nam et vinctis compassi estis, et rapinam bonorum vestrorum cum gaudio suscepistis. His ergo similia Thessalonicenses perpessi sunt a civibus suis.
paras.en: Moreover he praises the patience and constancy of the Thessalonians. [[2:14|For you, brethren, are become followers of the churches of God which are in Judea|Vos enim imitatores facti estis, fratres, Ecclesiarum Dei quæ sunt in Judæa]], that is, of the Jews faithful to Christ, who are founded [[2:14|in Christ Jesus|in Christo Jesu]]. For the primitive Church gathered in Judea was of the most perfect manner of life: therefore it was the exemplar or pattern of living for the other Churches. In what they imitated them, he adds: [[2:14|for you also have suffered the same things|quia eadem in specie, id est similia mala, passi estis et vos]] (the same in kind, that is, like evils) [[2:14|from your own countrymen|a contribulibus, id est concivibus vestris]] (that is, your fellow citizens), [[2:14|even as they have from the Jews|sicut et ipsi a Judæis]] who did not believe; that is, such things as the faithful Jews suffered from the unbelieving Jews. For, as we read in the Acts, when Stephen had been slain, [[Acts 8:1|there was raised a great persecution against the church which was at Jerusalem|facta est persecutio magna in Ecclesia Jerosolymitana]], and the unbelieving Jews seized the goods of the faithful. Of this persecution it is written to the Hebrews: [[Heb 10:32|But call to mind the former days, wherein|Rememoramini autem pristinos dies, in quibus]] [[Heb 10:32|you endured a great fight of afflictions|magnum sustinuistis certamen passionum]][[Heb 10:33||]]: [[Heb 10:34|For you both had compassion on them that were in bands and took with joy the being stripped of your own goods|nam et vinctis compassi estis, et rapinam bonorum vestrorum cum gaudio suscepistis]]. Things like these, then, the Thessalonians suffered from their fellow citizens.

paras.t: Qui infideles Judæi et Dominum occiderunt Jesum, quoniam mortem ejus procuraverunt a præside, et Prophetas quosdam novi Testamenti, multos quoque veteris Testamenti Prophetas occiderunt. Non tamen iidem numero occiderunt Christum et illos Prophetas. Sed loquitur de Judæis communiter, prout omnes perversi, sunt una generatio. Juxta quem modum ait Salvator in Evangelio ad Judæos: Veniet super vos omnis sanguis justus, etc.; et sequitur: Zachariæ, quem occidistis inter templum et altare. Hinc etiam in Actibus Apostolorum, Stephanus loquens Judæis: Patres, inquit, vestri occiderunt eos qui annuntiaverunt de adventu Justi, cujus vos nunc proditores et homicidæ fuistis. Et nos apostolos ac primitivam Ecclesiam persecuti sunt: ut patet in Actibus. Unde dixit Christus Apostolis: Si me persecuti sunt, et vos persequentur. Et Deo non placent. Impossibile quippe est sine fide placere Deo. Unde apud Jeremiam Christus testatur: Facta est mihi hereditas mea quasi leo in silva; dedit contra me vocem suam, ideo odivi eam. Et in Osee: Exosos habui eos propter malitiam adinventionum ipsorum; non addam ut diligam eos. Et omnibus hominibus adversantur, id est, omnium salutem impedire conantur.
paras.en: [[2:15|Who both killed the Lord Jesus|Qui infideles Judæi et Dominum occiderunt Jesum]], that is, the unbelieving Jews, since they procured his death from the governor[[Matt 27:1||]][[Matt 27:2||]][[Matt 27:26||]], [[2:15|and the prophets|et Prophetas]]: some prophets of the New Testament, and many prophets of the Old Testament too, they killed. Yet it was not the same men in number who killed Christ and those prophets. But he speaks of the Jews in common, inasmuch as all the perverse are one generation. In the same way the Saviour says in the Gospel to the Jews: [[Matt 23:35|That upon you may come all the just blood|Veniet super vos omnis sanguis justus]], etc.; and it goes on: of Zacharias, [[Matt 23:35|whom you killed between the temple and the altar|quem occidistis inter templum et altare]]. Hence too in the Acts of the Apostles Stephen, speaking to the Jews: Your fathers, he says, [[Acts 7:52|have slain them who foretold of the coming of the Just One: of whom you have been now the betrayers and murderers|occiderunt eos qui annuntiaverunt de adventu Justi, cujus vos nunc proditores et homicidæ fuistis]]. [[2:15|and have persecuted us|Et nos]], the apostles and the primitive Church, [[2:15|persecuted|persecuti sunt]]: as is plain in the Acts. Hence Christ said to the Apostles: [[John 15:20|If they have persecuted me, they will also persecute you|Si me persecuti sunt, et vos persequentur]] [the margin gives only John xv]. [[2:15|and please not God|Et Deo non placent]]. For [[Heb 11:6|without faith it is impossible to please God|Impossibile quippe est sine fide placere Deo]]. Hence in Jeremias Christ testifies: [[Jer 12:8|My inheritance is become to me as a lion in the wood: it hath cried out against me, therefore have I hated it|Facta est mihi hereditas mea quasi leo in silva; dedit contra me vocem suam, ideo odivi eam]]. And in Osee: [[Osee 9:15|I hated them: for the wickedness of their devices|Exosos habui eos propter malitiam adinventionum ipsorum]]; [[Osee 9:15|I will love them no more|non addam ut diligam eos]]. [[2:15|and are adversaries to all men|Et omnibus hominibus adversantur]], that is, they try to hinder the salvation of all.

paras.t: Prohibentes nos gentibus loqui verbum Christi, ut salvæ fiant credendo in Filium Dei, ut impleant prædicti Judæi peccata sua semper, id est, incessanter peccatis peccata adjiciant, donec in illis miserabiliter consumantur. Pervenit enim ira Dei, id est ultio divinæ justitiæ, scilicet excæcatio et obstinatio cordis eorum, captivitas quoque per Romanos inflicta, super eos, usque in finem sæculi duratura, juxta illud Danielis: Civitatem et sanctuarium dissipabit populus cum duce venturo, et finis ejus vastitas, et usque in finem perseverabit desolatio. Hæc quoque regius Psaltes apertissime cecinit: Obscurentur, inquiens, oculi eorum ne videant, et dorsum eorum semper incurva; effunde super eos iram tuam, et furor iræ tuæ comprehendat eos. Unde in Isaia ait Salvator: Calcavi eos in furore meo, et conculcavi eos in ira mea.
paras.en: [[2:16|Prohibiting us to speak to the Gentiles|Prohibentes nos gentibus loqui]] the word of Christ, [[2:16|that they may be saved|ut salvæ fiant]] by believing in the Son of God, [[2:16|to fill up their sins always|ut impleant prædicti Judæi peccata sua semper]], namely the said Jews; that is, that they may ceaselessly add sins to sins, until they are wretchedly consumed in them. [[2:16|for the wrath of God is come|Pervenit enim ira Dei]], that is, the vengeance of divine justice, namely the blinding and hardening of their heart, and also the captivity inflicted by the Romans, [[2:16|upon them to the end|super eos, usque in finem]] of the world, lasting according to that word of Daniel: [[Dan 9:26|a people, with their leader, that shall come, shall destroy the city, and the sanctuary: and the end thereof shall be waste|Civitatem et sanctuarium dissipabit populus cum duce venturo, et finis ejus vastitas]], [[Dan 9:27|and the desolation shall continue even to the consummation, and to the end|et usque in finem perseverabit desolatio]]. These things the royal Psalmist too sang most plainly, saying: [[Ps 68:24|Let their eyes be darkened that they see not; and their back bend thou down always|Obscurentur, inquiens, oculi eorum ne videant, et dorsum eorum semper incurva]]; [[Ps 68:25|Pour out thy indignation upon them: and let thy wrathful anger take hold of them|effunde super eos iram tuam, et furor iræ tuæ comprehendat eos]] [the margin gives Ps. lxix, 24, 25, Ps 68 in the Vulgate numbering]. Hence the Saviour says in Isaias: [[Is 63:3|I have trampled on them in my indignation, and have trodden them down in my wrath|Calcavi eos in furore meo, et conculcavi eos in ira mea]].

paras.t: Nos autem, o fratres, desolati a vobis, id est vestræ præsentiæ consolatione privati, ad tempus: privati, inquam, vestra præsentia, ore, adspectu, id est quantum ad vocalem collocutionem et corporalem adspectum, non corde, id est non quantum ad copulam caritatis: nam et spiritu præsens sum vobis, et dilectione intimus; abundantius solito festinavimus faciem vestram videre, id est vobis corporaliter præsentes adesse, cum multo desiderio:
paras.en: [[2:17|But we, brethren, being taken away from you|Nos autem, o fratres, desolati a vobis]], that is, deprived of the comfort of your presence [*desolati*, literally “made desolate”], [[2:17|for a short time|ad tempus]]: deprived, I say, of your presence [[2:17|in sight|ore, adspectu]] [Denis reads *ore, adspectu*, “in mouth, in sight,” where the Vulgate has *horæ, aspectu*], that is, as to talking together by voice and seeing with the body, [[2:17|not in heart|non corde]], that is, not as to the bond of charity: for I am present with you in spirit too, and close to you by love; [[2:17|have hastened the more abundantly|abundantius solito festinavimus]] than usual [[2:17|to see your face|faciem vestram videre]], that is, to be with you, present in the body, [[2:17|with great desire|cum multo desiderio]]:

paras.t: quoniam voluimus venire ad vos, quia audivimus vos in tot persecutionibus constitutos, propter quod optavimus vos roborare in Domino, ego quidem Paulus et semel et iterum, id est, bis, ex quo recessi a vobis, tentavi reverti ad vos; sed impedivit nos Satanas Deo permittente, id est, aliquam nobis occupationem procuravit, per quam impediti sumus venire ad vos.
paras.en: [[2:18|For we would have come unto you|quoniam voluimus venire ad vos]], because we heard that you were set in so many persecutions, for which reason we wished to strengthen you in the Lord, [[2:18|I Paul indeed, once and again|ego quidem Paulus et semel et iterum]], that is, twice since I left you I have tried to return to you; [[2:18|but Satan hath hindered us|sed impedivit nos Satanas]], God permitting, that is, he contrived some business for us, by which we were hindered from coming to you.

paras.t: Nec mirum quod voluimus venire ad vos: Quæ est enim spes nostra, id est materia nostræ fiduciæ, qua confidimus fructuosam esse nostram prædicationem in merito ac præmio, aut gaudium, id est materia nostræ consolationis in præsenti, aut corona gloriæ, id est ornamentum felicitatis nostræ futuræ? Nonne vos, discipuli nostri præclari, ex quorum sancta conversatione speramus fructuosum esse nostrum laborem, de quorum profectu gaudemus, de quorum etiam beatificatione gloriaturi, copiosiusque glorificandi sumus? Vos itaque estis hæc omnia nobis ante Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, id est coram Christo: quod maxime apparebit, in adventu ejus in die judicii.
paras.en: Nor is it any wonder that we wished to come to you: [[2:19|For what is our hope|Quæ est enim spes nostra]], that is, the ground of our confidence, by which we trust that our preaching is fruitful in merit and reward, [[2:19|or joy|aut gaudium]], that is, the ground of our consolation at present, [[2:19|or crown of glory|aut corona gloriæ]], that is, the ornament of our future happiness? [[2:19|Are not you|Nonne vos]], our illustrious disciples, from whose holy life we hope our labour is fruitful, at whose progress we rejoice, in whose being made blessed we shall also glory and be the more abundantly glorified? You therefore are all these things to us [[2:19|in the presence of our Lord Jesus Christ|ante Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum]], that is, before Christ: which will appear most of all [[2:19|at his coming|in adventu ejus]] on the day of judgement.

paras.t: Vos enim estis gloria nostra: quemadmodum scriptum est, Filius sapiens est gloria patris. Nam de vestra fide ac perfectione gloriamur apud alias Ecclesias, proponentes vos eis in exemplum. Estis quoque et gaudium nostrum, id est materia nostræ consolationis in via, et augmentum jucunditatis nostræ in patria. Unde ait Ambrosius: Manifestum est quod perfectio discipulorum, gaudium et corona est magistrorum. Fructus namque magistri, obedientia est discipuli: cujus bona conversatio, coronam, Christo judice, dat magistro.
paras.en: [[2:20|For you are our glory|Vos enim estis gloria nostra]]: as it is written, A wise son is the glory of his father[[Prov 10:1||]] [the margin gives Prov. x, 1, where the Douay-Rheims has “A wise son maketh the father glad”]. For we glory in your faith and perfection before the other Churches, setting you before them as an example. You are also [[2:20|and joy|et gaudium]] to us, that is, the ground of our consolation on the way, and the increase of our gladness in the fatherland. Hence Ambrose says: It is manifest that the perfection of the disciples is the joy and crown of the masters. For the fruit of the master is the obedience of the disciple, whose good life, with Christ as judge, gives the master a crown.

3.title: EXPOSITIO CAPITULI TERTII : PROPTER QUOD NON SUSTINENTES AMPLIUS.
3.title_en: Exposition of the third chapter: For which cause, forbearing no longer.

paras.t: Locis divinæ Scripturæ facilibus immorandum non reor, nisi forte uberem moralitatem contineant. Nunc ergo in locis epistolarum historicis atque facilibus celerius transibo.
paras.en: I do not think one should linger over the easy places of divine Scripture, unless perhaps they contain a rich moral teaching. So now I shall pass more quickly through the historical and easy places of the Epistles.

paras.t: Propter quod, videlicet quoniam tantum diligimus vos, non sustinentes amplius, id est diutius non differentes nostræ caritatis affectum vobis ostendere, placuit nobis, id est mihi et Silvano, remanere Athenis gratia prædicationis, solis, id est mihi et Silvano (ut dictum est), aliis discipulis ad diversa loca destinatis. Et misimus Timotheum fratrem nostrum, et ministrum Dei in Evangelio Christi prædicando, ad confirmandos vos in persecutionibus constitutos, et exhortandos vos pro fide vestra firmanda, id est, quatenus roboremini semper in fide, cujus firmitas omnium virtutum actus confortat; ut nemo vestrum moveatur, per impatientiam aut pusillanimitatem, in tribulationibus istis præsentibus et transitoriis, quæ non sunt condignæ ad futuram gloriam. Nam supra modum æternum gloriæ pondus operantur in nobis. Hinc ait Psalmista : Qui tribulant me, exsultabunt si motus fuero. Et Petrus ait in Canonica sua prima : Communicantes Christi passionibus gaudete, ut et in revelatione gloriæ ejus gaudeatis.
paras.en: [[3:1|For which cause|Propter quod]], namely, because we love you so much, [[3:1|forbearing no longer|non sustinentes amplius]], that is, no longer putting off showing you the affection of our charity, [[3:1|we thought it good|placuit nobis]], that is, Silvanus and me, [[3:1|to remain at Athens|remanere Athenis]] for the sake of preaching, [[3:1|alone|solis]], that is, Silvanus and I (as has been said), the other disciples having been sent off to different places. [[3:2|And we sent Timothy, our brother and the minister of God in the gospel of Christ|Et misimus Timotheum fratrem nostrum, et ministrum Dei in Evangelio Christi]] by preaching, [[3:2|to confirm you|ad confirmandos vos]], set as you are amid persecutions, [[3:2|and exhort you concerning your faith|et exhortandos vos pro fide vestra]], that it may be made firm: that is, so that you may always be strengthened in the faith, whose firmness gives strength to the acts of all the virtues; [[3:3|That no man should be moved|ut nemo vestrum moveatur]] through impatience or faint-heartedness [[3:3|in these tribulations|in tribulationibus istis]], present and passing, which [[Rom 8:18|are not worthy to be compared with the glory to come|non sunt condignæ ad futuram gloriam]]. For they work in us, [[2 Cor 4:17|above measure, exceedingly an eternal weight of glory|supra modum æternum gloriæ pondus]]. Hence the Psalmist says: [[Ps 12:5|They that trouble me, will rejoice when I am moved|Qui tribulant me, exsultabunt si motus fuero]]. And Peter says in his first Canonical Epistle: [[1 Pet 4:13|if you partake of the sufferings of Christ, rejoice that, when his glory shall be revealed, you may also be glad|Communicantes Christi passionibus gaudete, ut et in revelatione gloriæ ejus gaudeatis]].

paras.t: Ipsi enim scitis quod in hoc, id est ad sustinendum adversa, positi sumus in isto exsilio : quia per multas tribulationes oportet nos intrare regnum cælorum. Propterea scriptum est : Hæc est gratia, si propter Dei conscientiam sustinet quis tristitias, patiens injuste : in hoc enim vocati estis. Nam et quum apud vos essemus, prædicebamus vobis passuros nos tribulationes ab hominibus impiis propter justitiam, sicut et factum est, et scitis verum esse quod diximus, jamque impletum est.
paras.en: [[3:3|for yourselves know|Ipsi enim scitis]] that [[3:3|thereunto|in hoc]], that is, to endure adversities, [[3:3|we are appointed|positi sumus]] in this exile: for [[Acts 14:21|through many tribulations we must enter into the kingdom of God|per multas tribulationes oportet nos intrare regnum cælorum]] [Denis has "the kingdom of heaven", *regnum cælorum*, where the Vulgate has "the kingdom of God"]. Therefore it is written: [[1 Pet 2:19|this is thankworthy: if, for conscience towards God, a man endure sorrows, suffering wrongfully|Hæc est gratia, si propter Dei conscientiam sustinet quis tristitias, patiens injuste]] [*gratia*, "grace", which the Douay-Rheims renders "thankworthy"]: [[1 Pet 2:21|For unto this are you called|in hoc enim vocati estis]]. [[3:4|For even when we were with you, we foretold you that we should suffer tribulations|Nam et quum apud vos essemus, prædicebamus vobis passuros nos tribulationes]] from wicked men for justice' sake, [[3:4|as also it is come to pass, and you know|sicut et factum est, et scitis]] that what we said is true and is now fulfilled.

paras.t: Propterea, scilicet, ne moveamini in tribulationibus istis, et ego amplius non sustinens, id est diutius differre non valens vestrum statum percipere, propter ardentem amorem, qui facit sollicitum ipsum amantem de præcavendis amati periculis, misi Timotheum ad vos dudum antequam scripsi ; vel, Misi præsentem epistolam ; ad cognoscendum fidem vestram, id est, ut ab eo redeunte percipiam fidei vestræ stabilitatem, de qua certificari anxius cupio ; ne forte tentaverit, id est, impugnaverit sive deceperit, vos is qui tentat, id est diabolus, cujus officium est tentare, et inanis fiat labor noster, id est, prædicatio nostra infructuosa fiat, quantum ad vos, quamvis nobis infructuosa esse non poterit.
paras.en: [[3:5|For this cause|Propterea]], namely, lest you be moved in these tribulations, [[3:5|also, I, forbearing no longer|et ego amplius non sustinens]], that is, being unable to put off any longer learning how you stand, because of the burning love which makes the lover anxious to forestall the dangers of the beloved, [[3:5|sent|misi]] Timothy to you some while before I wrote; or, I [[3:5|sent|Misi]] the present letter; [[3:5|to know your faith|ad cognoscendum fidem vestram]], that is, so that from him on his return I may learn the steadfastness of your faith, of which I anxiously long to be assured; [[3:5|lest perhaps|ne forte]] [[3:5|he that tempteth|is qui tentat]], that is, the devil, whose office is to tempt, [[3:5|should have tempted you|tentaverit]], that is, assailed or deceived you, [[3:5|and our labour should be made vain|et inanis fiat labor noster]], that is, our preaching should be made fruitless as far as you are concerned, though for us it could not be fruitless.

paras.t: Nunc autem, quum præsentem dicto aut mitto epistolam, veniente Timotheo, quem dudum ante editionem epistolæ hujus ad vos misi, ad nos a vobis, et annuntiante nobis fidem et caritatem vestram, id est perfectionem et opera fidei caritatisque vestræ, et quia memoriam nostri habetis bonam, id est sinceram ac nobis perutilem, semper desiderantes nos videre oculo corporali, sicut nos quoque vos videre optamus ; ideo consolati sumus, fratres, in vobis, id est in consideratione perfectionis et gratiæ vestræ, vestroque profectu ex animo congaudemus, in omni necessitate, id est penuria, et tribulatione nostra : consolati, inquam, per fidem vestram, id est de fidei vestræ stabilitate, quod […] stabiliter et jucunde, si vos statis in Domino, firmiter adhærentes Deo per fidem, dilectionem et fortitudinem cordis.
paras.en: [[3:6|But now|Nunc autem]], as I dictate or send the present letter, [[3:6|when Timothy came|veniente Timotheo]] (whom I sent to you some while before this letter was issued) [[3:6|to us from you and related to us your faith and charity|ad nos a vobis, et annuntiante nobis fidem et caritatem vestram]], that is, the perfection and the works of your faith and charity, [[3:6|and that you have a good remembrance of us|et quia memoriam nostri habetis bonam]], that is, a sincere one and most profitable to us, [[3:6|always, desiring to see us|semper desiderantes nos videre]] with the bodily eye, [[3:6|as we also|sicut nos quoque]] long [[3:6|to see you|vos videre]]: [[3:7|Therefore we were comforted, brethren, in you|ideo consolati sumus, fratres, in vobis]], that is, in considering your perfection and grace, and we rejoice from our hearts at your progress, [[3:7|in all our necessity|in omni necessitate]], that is, want, [[3:7|and tribulation|et tribulatione nostra]]: comforted, I say, [[3:7|by your faith|per fidem vestram]], that is, by the steadfastness of your faith, because […] steadfastly and joyfully, [[3:8|if you stand in the Lord|si vos statis in Domino]], cleaving firmly to God by faith, love and strength of heart.

paras.t: Et merito consolati sumus : Quam enim gratiarum actionem possumus Deo retribuere pro vobis, nos constituti in omni gaudio spirituali, quo gaudemus propter vos, id est propter beneficia vobis collata, gaudemus autem ante Dominum nostrum, id est in conspectu divino, videlicet juste et religiose et in divinæ præsentiæ luce constituendo nos ipsos? quasi dicat : Dignas et sufficientes rependere gratiarum actiones non possumus, quia de vestris sicut […] de propriis gloriamur profectibus. Nocte ac die, id est certis horis diei noctisque, abundantius, id est plus solito, orantes Deum, ut videamus facies vestras, id est, ut dirigat Deus viam nostram ad vos, et compleamus ea quæ desunt fidei vestræ, id est, notitiam Scripturarum qua fides perficitur, plenius vobis jam imprimamus, quoniam capaciores nunc estis quam olim.
paras.en: And rightly are we comforted: [[3:9|For what thanks can we return to God for you|Quam enim gratiarum actionem possumus Deo retribuere pro vobis]], we who are set [[3:9|in all the joy|in omni gaudio]], spiritual joy, [[3:9|wherewith we rejoice for you|quo gaudemus propter vos]], that is, for the benefits bestowed on you; and we rejoice [[3:9|before our God|ante Dominum nostrum]] [Denis reads *Dominum*, "Lord", where the Vulgate has *Deum*, "God"], that is, in the sight of God, namely by setting ourselves justly and devoutly in the light of the divine presence? As if to say: we cannot render worthy and sufficient thanks, for we glory in your progress as […] in our own. [[3:10|Night and day|Nocte ac die]], that is, at fixed hours of the day and night, [[3:10|more abundantly|abundantius]], that is, more than usual, [[3:10|praying|orantes]] to God [[3:10|that we may see your face|ut videamus facies vestras]], that is, that God may direct our way to you, [[3:10|and may accomplish those things that are wanting to your faith|et compleamus ea quæ desunt fidei vestræ]]: that is, that we may now imprint on you more fully the knowledge of the Scriptures, by which faith is perfected, since you are now more capable of it than before.

paras.t: Ipse autem Deus et Pater, id est Pater æternus, et Dominus Jesus Christus, qui sunt unus director, dirigat viam nostram, […] id est gressum pedum nostrorum, ad vos.
paras.en: [[3:11|Now God himself and our Father|Ipse autem Deus et Pater]], that is, the eternal Father, [[3:11|and our Lord Jesus Christ|et Dominus Jesus Christus]], who are one director, [[3:11|direct our way|dirigat viam nostram]], […] that is, the steps of our feet, [[3:11|unto you|ad vos]].

paras.t: Vos autem Dominus multiplicet merito et numero, et abundare faciat caritatem vestram in invicem et in omnes, id est, hoc tribuat vobis, ut ferventer diligatis mutuo et ceteros omnes, quemadmodum Deus fecit et nos caritate abundare in vobis : ad confirmanda, id est, ut caritative confirmemus, corda vestra, ut sint sine querela in sanctitate, id est irreprehensibiliter sancta, ante Deum et Patrem nostrum, non solum coram hominibus qui decipi possunt ; et ut talia inveniantur in adventu Domini nostri Jesu Christi cum omnibus Sanctis ejus, id est in die judicii, quando Salvator venturus est cum omnibus cœli civibus ad finale judicium, sicut in Isaia legitur : Dominus ad judicium veniet cum senioribus populi sui et principibus ejus ; et in Zacharia, Veniet Dominus Deus meus, omnesque Sancti ejus cum eo. Unde et Judas in sua ait Canonica : Ecce veniet Dominus in sanctis millibus suis facere judicium, et arguere omnes impios. Amen.
paras.en: [[3:12|And may the Lord multiply you|Vos autem Dominus multiplicet]] in merit and in number, [[3:12|and make you abound in charity towards one another and towards all men|et abundare faciat caritatem vestram in invicem et in omnes]], that is, grant you this, that you love one another fervently, and all others too, [[3:12|as|quemadmodum]] God has made us also abound in charity [[3:12|towards you|in vobis]]: [[3:13|To confirm|ad confirmanda]], that is, so that we may confirm in charity, [[3:13|your hearts|corda vestra]], that they may be [[3:13|without blame, in holiness|sine querela in sanctitate]], that is, irreproachably holy, [[3:13|before God and our Father|ante Deum et Patrem nostrum]], and not only before men, who can be deceived; and that they may be found such [[3:13|at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, with all his saints|in adventu Domini nostri Jesu Christi cum omnibus Sanctis ejus]], that is, on the day of judgement, when the Saviour is to come with all the citizens of heaven to the final judgement, as we read in Isaias: [[Is 3:14|The Lord will enter into judgment with the ancients of his people, and its princes|Dominus ad judicium veniet cum senioribus populi sui et principibus ejus]]; and in Zacharias: [[Zach 14:5|the Lord my God shall come, and all the saints with him|Veniet Dominus Deus meus, omnesque Sancti ejus cum eo]]. Hence Jude too says in his Canonical Epistle: [[Jude 1:14|Behold, the Lord cometh with thousands of his saints|Ecce veniet Dominus in sanctis millibus suis]] [[Jude 1:15|To execute judgment upon all and to reprove all the ungodly|facere judicium, et arguere omnes impios]]. [[3:13|Amen|Amen]].

4.title: EXPOSITIO CAPITULI QUARTI : DE CETERO ERGO, FRATRES, ROGAMUS VOS ET OBSECRAMUS, ETC.
4.title_en: Exposition of the fourth chapter: For the rest therefore, brethren, we pray and beseech you, etc.

paras.t: Commendatione perfectorum inducta, descendit Apostolus ad specialem instructionem imperfectorum. Quamvis enim Ecclesia Thessalonicensium pro majori parte fuerit virtutibus probata, quidam tamen eorum certis vitiis servierunt, quos præsenti capitulo Apostolus corrigit et informat: primo, fornicarios. Gentiles quippe fornicationem simplicem reputaverunt licitam: propter quod quidam eorum, etiam post conversionem, proni erant ex pristina consuetudine ad fornicationem.
paras.en: Having set out his commendation of the perfect, the Apostle comes down to a particular instruction of the imperfect. For although the Church of the Thessalonians was for the greater part proved in the virtues, some of them were nevertheless slaves to certain vices; and these the Apostle corrects and instructs in the present chapter: first, the fornicators. For the Gentiles reckoned simple fornication [that is, intercourse between a man and a woman who are both unmarried] to be lawful; and for this reason some of them, even after their conversion, were prone to fornication from their former habit.

paras.t: Ait ergo sanctus Apostolus: De cetero ergo, fratres, id est, quoniam tantas pro vobis Domino gratiarum actiones et preces obtulimus, proinde rogamus vos, et obsecramus, id est, per sacrorum commemorationem precamur, in Domino Jesu, id est secundum voluntatem et institutionem Christi, ut quemadmodum accepistis, id est didicistis, a nobis sermone et opere, quomodo vos oportet ambulare, id est, quam timorate et reverenter necesse sit vobis Deo servire, ambulando per arctam viam quæ ducit ad vitam, et placere Deo per quotidianum profectum, sic et ambuletis, id est, taliter ambuletis coram Domino, serviendo ei in sanctitate atque justitia cunctis diebus, per vias, observationes seu operationes mandatorum cœlestium; ut abundetis magis in spiritualibus divitiis, quæ sunt splendor gratiæ, virtutes atque scientiæ.
paras.en: The holy Apostle says, then: [[4:1|For the rest therefore, brethren|De cetero ergo, fratres]], that is, since we have offered such thanksgiving and prayers to the Lord for you, therefore we [[4:1|pray and beseech you|rogamus vos, et obsecramus]], that is, we entreat you by calling holy things to mind [*obsecrare*, "to beseech", is taken as *ob sacra*, "by holy things"], [[4:1|in the Lord Jesus|in Domino Jesu]], that is, according to the will and ordinance of Christ, [[4:1|that, as you have received|ut quemadmodum accepistis]], that is, have learned, from us by word and deed, [[4:1|how you ought to walk|quomodo vos oportet ambulare]], that is, how fearfully and reverently you must serve God, walking by the strait way that leadeth to life[[Matt 7:14||]], [[4:1|and to please God|et placere Deo]] by daily progress, [[4:1|so also you would walk|sic et ambuletis]], that is, that you would so walk before the Lord, serving him in holiness and justice all days[[Luke 1:74||]], in the ways, the observances or works, of the heavenly commandments; [[4:1|that you may abound the more|ut abundetis magis]] in spiritual riches, which are the splendour of grace, the virtues and the sciences.

paras.t: Denique ideo obsecro hæc: Scitis enim quæ præcepta dederim vobis, quum apud vos essem, per Dominum Jesum, id est Christo loquente ac præcipiente per me.
paras.en: Lastly, I beseech these things for this reason: [[4:2|For you know what precepts I have given to you|Scitis enim quæ præcepta dederim vobis]], when I was among you, [[4:2|by the Lord Jesus|per Dominum Jesum]], that is, with Christ speaking and commanding through me.

paras.t: Hæc est enim voluntas Dei, id est res placens Deo, vel mandatum, signum existens voluntatis divinæ antecedentis vel consequentis, sanctificatio vestra, id est purgatio a peccatis: prout a B. Petro inducitur, Patienter agit Dominus propter vos, nolens aliquem perire, sed omnes ad pœnitentiam reverti; ut abstineatis vos a fornicatione, quæ est mortale peccatum. Nam et qui fornicatur, peccat in proprium corpus.
paras.en: [[4:3|For this is the will of God|Hæc est enim voluntas Dei]], that is, a thing pleasing to God, or a commandment, which is a sign of the divine will, antecedent or consequent [the antecedent will is God's will considered in itself, as that all be saved; the consequent, his will in view of the circumstances, as of each one's deeds], [[4:3|your sanctification|sanctificatio vestra]], that is, cleansing from sins, as is brought forward by blessed Peter: The Lord [[2 Pet 3:9|dealeth patiently for your sake, not willing that any should perish, but that all should return to penance|Patienter agit Dominus propter vos, nolens aliquem perire, sed omnes ad pœnitentiam reverti]]; [[4:3|That you should abstain from fornication|ut abstineatis vos a fornicatione]], which is a mortal sin. For [[1 Cor 6:18|he that committeth fornication sinneth against his own body|qui fornicatur, peccat in proprium corpus]].

paras.t: Ut sciat scientia efficaci et virtuosa unusquisque vestrum vas suum, id est proprium corpus, possidere, ipsum per rationem regendo, ne possideamur ab eo, sensualitate rationi prævalente: possidere, inquam, in sanctificatione, id est virtutum et castitatis munditia, et honore, id est in statu honesto, carnalium vitiorum turpitudinem fugiendo;
paras.en: [[4:4|That every one of you should know|Ut sciat]], with an effective and virtuous knowledge, [[4:4|his vessel|unusquisque vestrum vas suum]], that is, his own body, [[4:4|how to possess|possidere]], ruling it by reason, lest we be possessed by it, with sensuality prevailing over reason: to possess it, I say, [[4:4|in sanctification|in sanctificatione]], that is, in the cleanness of the virtues and of chastity, [[4:4|and honour|et honore]], that is, in an honourable state, fleeing the foulness of the carnal vices;

paras.t: non in passione desiderii, id est non in carnali concupiscentia, ei consentiendo, vel eam opere exsequendo, sicut et gentes quæ ignorant Deum, loquendo de cognitione formata atque distincta. Nam etsi dicant se nosse Deum, tamen opere negant. Unde Galatis dictum est: Qui autem sunt Christi, carnem suam crucifixerunt cum vitiis et concupiscentiis. Apud Ecclesiasticum quoque orat vir sapiens: Aufer a me ventris concupiscentias, et concubitus concupiscentia non apprehendat me.
paras.en: [[4:5|Not in the passion of lust|non in passione desiderii]], that is, not in carnal concupiscence, by consenting to it or by carrying it out in deed, [[4:5|like the Gentiles that know not God|sicut et gentes quæ ignorant Deum]]: speaking of a formed and distinct knowledge [*cognitio formata*: a knowledge of God that has its full form, as faith "formed" by charity is distinguished from unformed faith]. For though they say that they know God, yet in deed they deny him[[Tit 1:16||]]. Hence it was said to the Galatians: [[Gal 5:24|And they that are Christ's have crucified their flesh, with the vices and concupiscences|Qui autem sunt Christi, carnem suam crucifixerunt cum vitiis et concupiscentiis]]. In Ecclesiasticus too the wise man prays: [[Ecclus 23:6|Take from me the greediness of the belly, and let not the lusts of the flesh take hold of me|Aufer a me ventris concupiscentias, et concubitus concupiscentia non apprehendat me]].

paras.t: Et ne quis supergrediatur, id est, alium violenter suppeditet, sive impie opprimat, neque circumveniat, id est decipiat, in negotio aliquo fratrem, id est proximum […]mus, id est, firmiter asseruimus. Scriptum est enim in Levitico: Non facies calumniam proximo tuo, nec vi opprimes eum. Et sicut Jacobus asserit, Judicium sine misericordia fiet ei qui non fecerit misericordiam: quanto magis ei qui fecerit fraudem aut violentiam?
paras.en: [[4:6|And that no man overreach|Et ne quis supergrediatur]], that is, violently tread another underfoot or wickedly oppress him, [[4:6|nor circumvent|neque circumveniat]], that is, deceive, [[4:6|his brother in business|in negotio aliquo fratrem]], that is, his neighbour […] [the rest of the comment on this verse is lost in the transcription; the surviving ending "-mus" is that of *testificati sumus*, "and have testified"], that is, we have firmly asserted. For it is written in Leviticus: [[Lev 19:13|Thou shalt not calumniate thy neighbour, nor oppress him by violence|Non facies calumniam proximo tuo, nec vi opprimes eum]]. And as James asserts, [[Jas 2:13|judgment without mercy to him that hath not done mercy|Judicium sine misericordia fiet ei qui non fecerit misericordiam]]: how much more to him who has done fraud or violence?

paras.t: Non enim vocavit nos Deus in immunditiam, id est ad hoc ut sordibus peccatorum contaminemur, sed in sanctificationem: juxta illud Zachariæ, Serviamus illi in sanctitate et justitia. Ideo in Deuteronomio Moyses loquitur: Perfectus et absque macula eris cum Domino Deo tuo. Similitudo quippe est causa amoris. Propterea sanctus Dominus Deus noster sanctos requirit ministros, secundum quod ait in Levitico: Nolite contaminare animas vestras. Ego enim sum Dominus Deus vester. Sancti estote, quoniam ego sanctus sum. Vult ergo clementissimus Deus, pater piissimus, ut ei in virtutibus assimilemur.
paras.en: [[4:7|For God hath not called us unto uncleanness|Non enim vocavit nos Deus in immunditiam]], that is, to be defiled with the filth of sins, [[4:7|but unto sanctification|sed in sanctificationem]]: according to that saying of Zachary, that [[Luke 1:74|we may serve him|Serviamus illi]] [[Luke 1:75|in holiness and justice|in sanctitate et justitia]]. Therefore Moses says in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 18:13|Thou shalt be perfect, and without spot before the Lord thy God|Perfectus et absque macula eris cum Domino Deo tuo]]. For likeness is the cause of love. For this reason the Lord our God, being holy, requires holy ministers, according to what he says in Leviticus: [[Lev 11:43|Do not defile your souls|Nolite contaminare animas vestras]]. [[Lev 11:44|For I am the Lord your God. Be holy because I am holy|Ego enim sum Dominus Deus vester. Sancti estote, quoniam ego sanctus sum]]. Most merciful God, then, our most loving Father, wills that we be made like him in the virtues.

paras.t: Itaque qui hæc præcepta spernit, non hominem spernit, id est, non solum me, vel alium Dei ministrum, ex parte Dei ista jubentem, contemnit seu vilipendit, non satagens obedire, sed Deum principaliter spernit seu inhonorat. Cui consonat quod apud Lucam ait Salvator: Qui vos audit, me audit; et qui vos spernit, me spernit. Unde et Moyses filiis Israel loquens: Non contra nos, inquit, est vestrum murmur, sed contra Deum. Christi ergo vicariis tanquam Christo, reverenter ac prompte obedire debemus. Qui etiam Pater vel Filius dedit Spiritum Sanctum suum in nobis, id est, cordibus nostris illum infudit, conferendo nobis dona ipsius: ut dictum aliis locis est plenius. Unde apud Romanos testatur: Caritas Dei diffusa est in cordibus nostris per Spiritum Sanctum, qui datus est nobis. Et apud Joannem Christus loquebatur discipulis: Ego rogabo Patrem, et alium Paracletum dabit […]
paras.en: [[4:8|Therefore, he that despiseth these things, despiseth not man|Itaque qui hæc præcepta spernit, non hominem spernit]] [Denis reads "these precepts"], that is, he does not despise or make light of me only, or of another minister of God who commands these things on God's behalf, when he does not take care to obey, [[4:8|but God|sed Deum]] he chiefly despises or dishonours. With this agrees what the Saviour says in Luke: [[Luke 10:16|He that heareth you heareth me: and he that despiseth you despiseth me|Qui vos audit, me audit; et qui vos spernit, me spernit]]. Hence Moses too, speaking to the children of Israel: [[Ex 16:8|your murmuring is not against us|Non contra nos]], he says, [[Ex 16:8|but against the Lord|est vestrum murmur, sed contra Deum]]. We ought therefore to obey the vicars of Christ reverently and promptly, as we would Christ. He also, the Father or the Son, [[4:8|hath given his holy Spirit in us|dedit Spiritum Sanctum suum in nobis]], that is, has poured him into our hearts by bestowing his gifts on us, as has been said more fully in other places. Hence he testifies to the Romans: [[Rom 5:5|the charity of God is poured forth in our hearts, by the Holy Ghost who is given to us|Caritas Dei diffusa est in cordibus nostris per Spiritum Sanctum, qui datus est nobis]]. And in John Christ said to the disciples: [[John 14:16|I will ask the Father: and he shall give you another Paraclete|Ego rogabo Patrem, et alium Paracletum dabit]] […] [the margin gives John 14:16, 17; the rest of the quotation, and the beginning of the comment on v. 9, are lost in the transcription]

paras.t: […]cesse habuimus scribere vobis perfectioribus; ipsi enim vos a Deo per Spiritus Sancti illustrationem didicistis: ut ait Joannes: Non necesse habetis ut aliquis vos doceat, sed unctio ejus docet vos de omnibus. Itaque didicistis a Deo, a quo qui eruditur, beatus est, ut diligatis invicem. Unde et magister Dominus noster: In hoc, inquit, cognoscent omnes quia discipuli mei estis, si dilectionem habueritis ad invicem. Etenim facitis illud in omnes fratres, id est, caritatis fraternæ affectum et opus fratribus cunctis impenditis, in universa Macedonia, cujus urbs vestra, metropolis est.
paras.en: […] [[4:9|we have no need to write to you|cesse habuimus scribere vobis]], who are more perfect; [[4:9|for yourselves|ipsi enim vos]], [[4:9|of God|a Deo]], through the enlightening of the Holy Ghost, [[4:9|have learned|didicistis]]; as John says: [[1 John 2:27|you have no need that any man teach you|Non necesse habetis ut aliquis vos doceat]]: but [[1 John 2:27|his unction teacheth you of all things|unctio ejus docet vos de omnibus]]. And so you have learned of God, by whom whoever is taught is blessed[[Ps 93:12||]], [[4:9|to love one another|ut diligatis invicem]]. Hence our Lord and master too: [[John 13:35|By this|In hoc]], he says, [[John 13:35|shall all men know that you are my disciples, if you have love one for another|cognoscent omnes quia discipuli mei estis, si dilectionem habueritis ad invicem]]. [[4:10|For indeed you do it towards all the brethren|Etenim facitis illud in omnes fratres]], that is, you bestow the affection and the work of brotherly charity on all the brethren, [[4:10|in all Macedonia|in universa Macedonia]], of which your city is the metropolis.
