paras.t: Rogamus autem vos, fratres, ut abundetis magis in dilectione ceterisque virtutibus, et operam detis, id est, diligentiam et conamen adhibeatis, ut quieti sitis, curiositatem et loquacitatem ac evagationes seu discursus vitando. Ait enim Deus sublimis apud Isaiam: Super quem requiescet Spiritus meus, nisi super quietum et humilem? Rursusque alibi apud eumdem: Si revertamini et quiescatis, salvi eritis; in silentio et spe erit fortitudo vestra. Denique bonum est cum silentio præstolari salutare Dei. Anima quoque, secundum Aristotelem, quiescendo fit prudens. Et ut vestrum negotium agatis, id est, quisque faciat quod ad se pertinet, nec cum alienis et impertinentibus causis se occupet, ut sit vobis caritas ordinata. Et operemini manibus vestris opera utilia. Otia enim dant vitia, juxta illud Ecclesiastici: Multam malitiam docuit otiositas. Hinc namque de impiis canit Psalmista: In labore hominum non sunt, et cum hominibus non flagellabuntur: ideo tenuit eos superbia, operti sunt iniquitate et impietate sua. Nec mirum, quia ut dicitur in Job, homo ad laborem nascitur, et avis ad volandum. Unde in Ezechiele legitur: Hæc fuit iniquitas Sodomæ, superbia, saturitas panis, et abundantia, et otium ejus. Itaque operamini, sicut præcepimus vobis. Et ut honeste ambuletis ad eos qui foris sunt, id est, coram extraneis exemplariter irreprehensibiliterque vivatis. Et nullius aliquid desideretis sine rationabili causa. Unde hoc verbo avaritia prohibetur, quemadmodum etiam in Exodo dicitur: Non concupisces rem proximi tui. His itaque verbis curiosi, inquieti seu vagabundi, et cupidi notantur ac corriguntur.
paras.en: [[4:10|But we entreat you, brethren, that you abound more|Rogamus autem vos, fratres, ut abundetis magis]] in love and the other virtues, [[4:11|And that you use your endeavour|et operam detis]], that is, apply diligence and effort, [[4:11|to be quiet|ut quieti sitis]], avoiding curiosity and talkativeness and wanderings or running about. For God on high says in Isaias: Upon whom shall my Spirit rest, but upon him that is quiet and humble?[[Is 66:2||]] [the margin reads "Is. lxxi, 1, 2", a misreading of lxvi; Denis quotes Is 66:2 in an older form, where the Douay-Rheims has "to whom shall I have respect, but to him that is poor and little, and of a contrite spirit"] And again elsewhere in the same: [[Is 30:15|If you return and be quiet, you shall be saved: in silence and in hope shall your strength be|Si revertamini et quiescatis, salvi eritis; in silentio et spe erit fortitudo vestra]]. Lastly, [[Lam 3:26|It is good to wait with silence for the salvation of God|bonum est cum silentio præstolari salutare Dei]]. The soul too, according to Aristotle, becomes prudent by being at rest. [[4:11|and that you do your own business|Et ut vestrum negotium agatis]], that is, that each do what belongs to him, and not busy himself with others' affairs that do not concern him, so that your charity may be ordered. [[4:11|and work with your own hands|Et operemini manibus vestris]] useful works. For idleness breeds vices [*otia dant vitia*, a proverb that rhymes in Latin], according to that saying of Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 33:29|idleness hath taught much evil|Multam malitiam docuit otiositas]]. For hence the Psalmist sings of the wicked: [[Ps 72:5|They are not in the labour of men: neither shall they be scourged like other men|In labore hominum non sunt, et cum hominibus non flagellabuntur]]: [[Ps 72:6|Therefore pride hath held them fast: they are covered with their iniquity and their wickedness|ideo tenuit eos superbia, operti sunt iniquitate et impietate sua]]. Nor is it any wonder, since, as is said in Job, [[Job 5:7|Man is born to labour, and the bird to fly|homo ad laborem nascitur, et avis ad volandum]]. Hence we read in Ezechiel: [[Ezech 16:49|this was the iniquity of Sodom|Hæc fuit iniquitas Sodomæ]], [[Ezech 16:49|pride, fulness of bread, and abundance, and the idleness of her|superbia, saturitas panis, et abundantia, et otium ejus]]. So then, work, [[4:11|as we commanded you|sicut præcepimus vobis]]. [[4:11|and that you walk honestly towards them that are without|Et ut honeste ambuletis ad eos qui foris sunt]], that is, that you live in an exemplary and blameless way before outsiders. [[4:11|and that you want nothing of any man's|Et nullius aliquid desideretis]] without reasonable cause [Latin *desideretis*, which Denis takes as "desire"; hence what he says of avarice]. Hence by this word avarice is forbidden, just as is said in Exodus too: [[Ex 20:17|Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's|Non concupisces rem proximi tui]] goods. By these words, then, the curious, the restless or vagabond, and the covetous are censured and corrected.

paras.t: Consequenter docet Apostolus eos qui de futura resurrectione minus plene sperabant, atque ob hoc de amicorum suorum morte immoderate dolebant, ac si omnino perissent. Itaque ait: Nolo autem vos ignorare, fratres, fidei veritatem de dormientibus, id est defunctis: qui per comparationem ad divinam virtutem, dormire censentur, quia facilius a Deo suscitabuntur, quam dormiens ab homine excitetur. Unde apud Danielem Gabriel: Multi, inquit, de his qui dormiunt in pulvere terræ, evigilabunt. Hinc etiam Christus apud Joannem loquitur: Lazarus amicus noster dormit, sed vado ut a somno suscitem illum. Loquitur autem Scriptura de quadruplici dormitione seu somno, videlicet: de somno naturæ quotidiano ac solito, de quo in Marco legimus: Erat Jesus in puppi super cervical dormiens. De somno culpæ, de quo ad Romanos: Tempus est jam nos de somno surgere. De somno mortis, sicut in libris Regum de unoquoque pene habetur: Dormivit cum patribus suis. De somno item contemplationis, de quo in Genesi: Misit Dominus soporem in Adam; et in Canticis, Somnus meus dulcis gutturi meo.
paras.en: Next the Apostle teaches those who hoped less fully in the future resurrection, and for that reason grieved immoderately at the death of their friends, as if they had perished altogether. So he says: [[4:12|And we will not have you ignorant brethren|Nolo autem vos ignorare, fratres]] [Denis reads *Nolo*, "I will not"; the margin notes the reading *Nolumus*, "we will not"], of the truth of the faith [[4:12|concerning them that are asleep|de dormientibus]], that is, the dead: who, in comparison with the divine power, are reckoned to be asleep, because they will be raised by God more easily than a sleeper is roused by a man. Hence Gabriel in Daniel: [[Dan 12:2|many|Multi]], he says, [[Dan 12:2|of those that sleep in the dust of the earth, shall awake|de his qui dormiunt in pulvere terræ, evigilabunt]]. Hence too Christ says in John: [[John 11:11|Lazarus our friend sleepeth: but I go that I may awake him out of sleep|Lazarus amicus noster dormit, sed vado ut a somno suscitem illum]]. Now Scripture speaks of a fourfold falling asleep, or sleep: namely, of the daily and customary sleep of nature, of which we read in Mark: Jesus [[Mark 4:38|was in the hinder part of the ship, sleeping upon a pillow|Erat Jesus in puppi super cervical dormiens]]; of the sleep of sin, of which to the Romans: [[Rom 13:11|it is now the hour for us to rise from sleep|Tempus est jam nos de somno surgere]]; of the sleep of death, as is said of almost every one in the books of Kings: He [[3 Kings 2:10|slept with his fathers|Dormivit cum patribus suis]] [no margin reference; the formula recurs throughout the books of Kings, as at 3 Kings 2:10]; and likewise of the sleep of contemplation, of which in Genesis: [[Gen 2:21|the Lord God cast a deep sleep upon Adam|Misit Dominus soporem in Adam]]; and in the Canticle, My sleep is sweet to my palate[[Cant 2:3||]] [the margin gives "cf. Cant. ii, 3", where it is the beloved's fruit that is sweet to the palate; "my sleep was sweet to me" is in Jer 31:26].

paras.t: Ut non contristemini de morte propinquorum et carorum vestrorum inordinate, ac si illi penitus esse desinerent, et nunquam eis reuniri possetis, sicut et ceteri tristantur qui spem futuræ resurrectionis non habent. Non enim pereunt nobis proximi nostri per mortem. Unde dicitur Deus sancto Job omnia reddidisse dupla, quamvis non habuerit plures filios ac filias post, quam ante. Nam et defuncti remanserunt denuo vivificandi. Possumus ergo, et aliquando debemus, de morte proximorum tristari ac flere: primo, propter naturalis pietatis affectum; secundo, propter monstrandum dilectionis indicium; tertio, ad consolationem aliorum; quarto, propter damnum quod incurrit Ecclesia ex morte justorum. Sic Ambrosius planxit devotos sacerdotes.
paras.en: [[4:12|that you be not sorrowful|Ut non contristemini]] inordinately over the death of your kinsfolk and dear ones, as if they had altogether ceased to be and you could never be united with them again, [[4:12|even as others|sicut et ceteri]] are sorrowful [[4:12|who have no hope|qui spem]] of the future resurrection. For our neighbours do not perish to us through death. Hence God is said to have given back to holy Job all things double, although he did not have more sons and daughters afterwards than before[[Job 42:10||]]; for the dead too remained, to be brought to life again. We may, then, and sometimes we ought to, grieve and weep at the death of our neighbours: first, from the affection of natural tenderness; secondly, to show a sign of love; thirdly, for the consolation of others; fourthly, because of the loss the Church incurs from the death of the just. So Ambrose mourned devout priests.

paras.t: Si enim credimus: quod utique necesse est credere: quod Jesus mortuus est die Parasceves, et resurrexit tertio die, ita credendum est quod et Deus Trinitas eos qui dormierunt, id est defuncti sunt, per Jesum, id est in fide et gratia Christi (qui obdormierunt in Domino, sicut et de Stephano scriptum est in Actibus apostolicis), adducet ad regnum cœleste, beatificatos in anima et corpore, cum eo, id est cum Christo, qui peracto judicio cum electis ascendet ad cœlos. Ideo apud Joannem ait: Pater, quos dedisti mihi, volo ut ubi sum ego, et illi sint mecum, ut videant claritatem meam. Vel, Adducet cum eo, quia electi qui interim moriuntur et glorificantur, simul cum Christo et in ejus ducatu ad judicium venient.
paras.en: [[4:13|For if we believe|Si enim credimus]], as indeed we must believe, [[4:13|that Jesus died|quod Jesus mortuus est]] on the day of the Parasceve [that is, the day of preparation, Good Friday], [[4:13|and rose again|et resurrexit]] on the third day, [[4:13|even so|ita]] it must be believed that [[4:13|them who have slept|eos qui dormierunt]], that is, who have died, [[4:13|through Jesus|per Jesum]], that is, in the faith and grace of Christ (who [[Acts 7:59|fell asleep in the Lord|obdormierunt in Domino]], as is written of Stephen too in the Acts of the Apostles), [[4:13|will God|et Deus]], the Trinity, [[4:13|bring|adducet]] to the heavenly kingdom, beatified in soul and body, [[4:13|with him|cum eo]], that is, with Christ, who, when the judgment is done, will ascend with the elect into heaven. Therefore he says in John: [[John 17:24|Father, I will that where I am, they also whom thou hast given me may be with me: that they may see my glory|Pater, quos dedisti mihi, volo ut ubi sum ego, et illi sint mecum, ut videant claritatem meam]]. Or, [[4:13|bring with him|Adducet cum eo]], because the elect who die and are glorified in the meantime will come to the judgment together with Christ and under his leadership.

paras.t: Insuper ponit Apostolus modum ac ordinem resurrectionis futuræ. Hoc vobis dicimus in verbo Domini, id est in doctrina Christi, videlicet sicut a Deo didicimus, nec proprio sermone utimur; quod nos qui vivimus, qui residui su[…], id est illi ex nostris qui in die judicii fuerint vivi inventi atque superstites, ita quod nec ab Antichristo, nec aliunde occisi sunt, in adventu Domini, id est Christo ad judicium descendente, non præveniemus eos, id est, non resurgemus […] ante eos, qui dormierunt, id est, qui longo tempore ante defuncti fuerunt. Omnes enim simul resurgent, quoniam resurrectio erit in instanti, aut certe in brevissimo tempore, sicut prædixit Apostolus: In momento, in ictu oculi. Commemorat autem se Apostolus illis qui tunc erunt, propter unitatem mystici corporis Christi: hac occasione scripsit eis secundam epistolam.
paras.en: Further, the Apostle sets out the manner and order of the future resurrection. [[4:14|this we say unto you in the word of the Lord|Hoc vobis dicimus in verbo Domini]], that is, in the teaching of Christ: namely, as we have learned it from God, and we are not using words of our own; [[4:14|that we who are alive, who remain|quod nos qui vivimus, qui residui]] […], that is, those of ours who on the day of judgment are found alive and surviving, so that they have not been slain by Antichrist or in any other way, [[4:14|unto the coming of the Lord|in adventu Domini]], that is, when Christ comes down to the judgment, [[4:14|shall not prevent them|non præveniemus eos]] [*prevent*: go before], that is, we shall not rise […] before them, [[4:14|who have slept|qui dormierunt]], that is, who died a long time before. For all will rise together, since the resurrection will be in an instant, or at least in the briefest time, as the Apostle foretold: [[1 Cor 15:52|In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye|In momento, in ictu oculi]]. Now the Apostle numbers himself with those who will be living then, on account of the unity of the mystical body of Christ: on this occasion he wrote them the second epistle [that is, it seems, because they took him to mean that the day of the Lord was at hand: cf. 2 Thess 2:2].

paras.t: Quod autem non præveniemus illos, secundum hunc sensum, hinc constat: Quoniam ipse Dominus Christus in jussu, id est actuali imperio, quo mortuorum resurrectionem jubebit, et in voce archangeli, id est facta a se ipso, qui est magni consilii Angelus, angelorumque princeps: de qua ait apud Joannem, Veniet hora, in qua omnes qui in monumentis sunt, audient vocem Filii Dei. Vel, In voce archangeli, id est Michaelis, qui est princeps et custos Ecclesiæ, qui Deo jubente dicturus est: Surgite, mortui, venite ad judicium. Multi autem angelorum ministerium exhibebunt circa mortuorum resurrectionem, cineres colligendo, suscitando, ad locum judicii deferendo, magnum quoque terrorem terribili voce impiis incutiendo. Propter quod in Matthæo legimus: Mittet angelos suos cum tuba. Unde jam subditur: et in tuba Dei, id est cum prædicta voce archangeli vel imperio Christi: quæ nomine tubæ designantur, quoniam alte et clare sonabunt; vel, propter similitudinem tubæ corporeæ veteris Testamenti, per quam Judæi congregabantur ad concilium, commovebantur ad prælium, vocabantur ad festum. Simili modo hac tuba resurgentes congregabuntur ad concilium judicii, ad prælium quoque quo orbis terrarum pugnabit contra insensatos, et ad solennitatem æternam. Descendet in propria persona atque visibili forma, de cœlo empyreo, juxta illud Apocalypsis: Ecce venit cum nubibus, et videbit eum omnis oculus, et qui eum pupugerunt.
paras.en: That we [[4:14|shall not prevent them|non præveniemus illos]], in this sense, is clear from this: [[4:15|For the Lord himself|Quoniam ipse Dominus]], Christ, [[4:15|with commandment|in jussu]], that is, with the actual command by which he will order the resurrection of the dead, [[4:15|and with the voice of an archangel|et in voce archangeli]], that is, uttered by himself, who is the Angel of great counsel[[Is 9:6||]] [the margin gives Is. ix, 6, "according to the Septuagint", which calls the child the "Angel of great counsel"; the Douay-Rheims, following the Vulgate, has "Counsellor"] and prince of the angels: of which voice he says in John, [[John 5:28|the hour cometh wherein all that are in the graves shall hear the voice of the Son of God|Veniet hora, in qua omnes qui in monumentis sunt, audient vocem Filii Dei]] [the margin gives John 5:25; the words are those of 5:28]. Or, [[4:15|with the voice of an archangel|In voce archangeli]], that is, of Michael, who is prince and guardian of the Church[[Dan 12:1||]], who at God's command will say: Arise, ye dead, come to the judgment. And many of the angels will render their ministry about the resurrection of the dead, gathering the ashes, raising them, carrying them to the place of judgment, and also striking great terror into the wicked with a terrible voice. For this reason we read in Matthew: [[Matt 24:31|he shall send his angels with a trumpet|Mittet angelos suos cum tuba]]. Hence there follows at once: [[4:15|and with the trumpet of God|et in tuba Dei]], that is, with the aforesaid voice of the archangel, or command of Christ, which are designated by the name of trumpet because they will sound loud and clear; or because of the likeness to the bodily trumpet of the Old Testament, by which the Jews were gathered to council, stirred to battle, and called to a feast. In like manner, by this trumpet those who rise will be gathered to the council of judgment, to the battle also in which [[Wis 5:21|the whole world shall fight with him against the unwise|orbis terrarum pugnabit contra insensatos]], and to the eternal solemnity. He [[4:15|shall come down|Descendet]] in his own person and in visible form, [[4:15|from heaven|de cœlo]], the empyrean [that is, the highest heaven, the dwelling of the blessed], according to that of the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 1:7|Behold, he cometh with the clouds, and every eye shall see him: and they also that pierced him|Ecce venit cum nubibus, et videbit eum omnis oculus, et qui eum pupugerunt]].

paras.t: Et mortui qui in Christo sunt, id est, qui interim in Christo per mortem quieverunt […]. Nos qui vivimus, id est, qui tunc vivi inveniuntur, qui relinquimur, id est, qui usque ad diem illum in vita dimittentur, et sic[…] quieverunt, in nubibus, quæ nos suscipient, sicut Christum ascendentem nubes suscepit, obviam Christo in aera: quia et nos in aerem transferemur sive levabimur, et Christus descendet in aerem super vallem Josaphat. Propter quod apud Matthæum inducitur: Media nocte clamor factus est, Ecce sponsus venit, exite obviam ei. Unde in Joele Deus loquitur: Consurgant et ascendant gentes in vallem Josaphat, quia ibi sedebo ut judicem omnes gentes in circuitu. Et sic semper, id est æternaliter, cum Domino erimus in patria, prolata illa sententia: Venite, benedicti Patris mei, percipite regnum quod vobis paratum est ab origine mundi.
paras.en: [[4:15|and the dead who are in Christ|Et mortui qui in Christo sunt]], that is, who in the meantime have rested in Christ through death […] [the comment on "shall rise first" seems to be lost in the transcription]. [[4:16|we who are alive|Nos qui vivimus]], that is, who are found alive then, [[4:16|who are left|qui relinquimur]], that is, who will be left in life until that day, and […] [part of the text is lost here in the transcription, where the comment on "shall be taken up together with them" stood] have rested, [[4:16|in the clouds|in nubibus]], which will receive us as a cloud received Christ ascending[[Acts 1:9||]], [[4:16|to meet Christ, into the air|obviam Christo in aera]]: because we too will be carried over or lifted up into the air, and Christ will come down into the air above the valley of Josaphat. For this reason it is brought forward in Matthew: [[Matt 25:6|at midnight there was a cry made: Behold the bridegroom cometh. Go ye forth to meet him|Media nocte clamor factus est, Ecce sponsus venit, exite obviam ei]]. Hence God says in Joel: [[Joel 3:12|Let them arise, and let the nations come up into the valley of Josaphat: for there I will sit to judge all nations round about|Consurgant et ascendant gentes in vallem Josaphat, quia ibi sedebo ut judicem omnes gentes in circuitu]]. [[4:16|and so shall we be always|Et sic semper]], that is, eternally, [[4:16|with the Lord|cum Domino erimus]] in the fatherland, when that sentence has been pronounced: [[Matt 25:34|Come, ye blessed of my Father, possess you the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world|Venite, benedicti Patris mei, percipite regnum quod vobis paratum est ab origine mundi]].

paras.t: Præterea magna est difficultas, quomodo intelligendus sit iste priorum hujusmodi ac posteriorum ordo, de quibus dicit Apostolus: Mortui qui in Christo sunt, resurgent primi; deinde nos qui vivimus, qui relinquimur. Nunc enim prædictum est, quod omnes mortui simul resurgent etiam in momento ictuque oculi: instantanea quippe erit resurrectio, quoad id quod fiet a Deo, videlicet quantum ad ipsam animæ et corporis reassociationem. Virtus enim divina, quum sit infinita, operatur in instanti. Quantum vero ad id quod fiet ministerio angelorum, scilicet quoad cin[…]
paras.en: Further, there is great difficulty in how this order of the first and the later is to be understood, of which the Apostle says: [[4:15|the dead who are in Christ shall rise first|Mortui qui in Christo sunt, resurgent primi]]; [[4:16|Then we who are alive, who are left|deinde nos qui vivimus, qui relinquimur]]. For it has just been said that all the dead will rise together, and that in a moment and the twinkling of an eye: for the resurrection will be instantaneous as to what will be done by God, namely as to the very reuniting of soul and body; for the divine power, since it is infinite, works in an instant. But as to what will be done by the ministry of the angels, namely as to […] [the rest of the article is lost in the transcription; the last word surviving begins *cin-*, probably *cineres*, "the ashes", which he has said the angels will gather]

4.note: Some passages of this article are lost in the transcription of the scan, and its end is missing; the gaps are marked […].

5.title_en: Exposition of the fifth chapter [the heading is lost in the transcription]

paras.t: […] constat (sicut subjungitur). Ipsi enim diligenter scitis, id est, cum magna advertentia cognoscitis, quia dies Domini, id est hora finalis judicii : quæ dicitur dies, non solum propter solis illustrationem, sed et propter omnium operum hominum manifestationem : tunc enim illuminabit Dominus abscondita tenebrarum; sicut fur in nocte, ita veniet, id est, latenter, improvise et subito accidet, sicut fur tempore noctis domum ingreditur; vel, Sicut fur, id est improvise, in nocte, ita veniet, id est, latenter adveniet, ad similitudinem furis. Unde in Matthæo legimus : Media nocte clamor factus est, Ecce sponsus venit.
paras.en: […] [the beginning of the article, with the gloss on verse 1 and the start of that on verse 2, is lost in the transcription] is clear (as is added next). [[5:2|For yourselves know perfectly|Ipsi enim diligenter scitis]], that is, you know with great attention, [[5:2|that the day of the Lord|quia dies Domini]], that is, the hour of the final judgement, which is called a day not only because of the sun's shining but also because all men's works will be made manifest: for then the Lord [[1 Cor 4:5|will bring to light the hidden things of darkness|illuminabit Dominus abscondita tenebrarum]]; [[5:2|shall so come as a thief in the night|sicut fur in nocte, ita veniet]], that is, it will happen secretly, unexpectedly and suddenly, as a thief enters a house in the night-time; or: [[5:2|as a thief|Sicut fur]], that is, unexpectedly, [[5:2|in the night|in nocte]], [[5:2|shall so come|ita veniet]], that is, it will come secretly, after the manner of a thief. Hence we read in Matthew: [[Matt 25:6|at midnight there was a cry made: Behold the bridegroom cometh|Media nocte clamor factus est, Ecce sponsus venit]].

paras.t: Quum enim dixerint impii : Pax nobis est, id est quies a malis præsentibus, et securitas a futuris periculis; tunc repentinus eis superveniet interitus, id est subitanea perditio diei judicii, sicut dolor in utero habentis, id est tam pœnalis, quam est cruciatus mulieris parturientis, et non effugient mortem et judicis manum.
paras.en: [[5:3|For when they shall say|Quum enim dixerint]], namely the wicked: [[5:3|Peace|Pax nobis est]] is ours [Denis reads *Pax nobis est*, "We have peace"], that is, rest from present evils, [[5:3|and security|et securitas]] from future dangers; [[5:3|then shall sudden destruction come upon them|tunc repentinus eis superveniet interitus]], that is, the sudden perdition of the day of judgement, [[5:3|as the pains upon her that is with child|sicut dolor in utero habentis]], that is, as painful as the torment of a woman in labour, [[5:3|and they shall not escape|et non effugient]] death and the hand of the judge.

paras.t: Istud ergo scitur de tempore et momento futuri judicii, quod improvise veniet, atque celerrime finietur, sicut apud Matthæum legimus : Sicut fulgur exit ab oriente, et apparet usque in occidentem, ita erit adventus Filii hominis. Quod vero de tempore et momento scire non potestis, videlicet determinatam horam ejus, et quantum distet, nec mihi Paulo apostolo innotescit. Propter quod ait Salvator in Actibus Apostolorum : Non est vestrum nosse tempora et momenta, quæ Pater posuit in sua potestate; et alibi, De die autem illa et hora nemo scit, neque angeli cœlorum.
paras.en: This, then, is known about the time and moment of the judgement to come: that it will come unexpectedly and be over very swiftly, as we read in Matthew: [[Matt 24:27|as lightning cometh out of the east and appeareth even into the west: so shall also the cowling of the Son of man be|Sicut fulgur exit ab oriente, et apparet usque in occidentem, ita erit adventus Filii hominis]]. But what you cannot know about the time and moment, namely its fixed hour and how far off it is, is not made known to me, Paul the apostle, either. For this reason the Saviour says in the Acts of the Apostles: [[Acts 1:7|It is not for you to know the time or moments, which the Father hath put in his own power|Non est vestrum nosse tempora et momenta, quæ Pater posuit in sua potestate]]; and elsewhere: [[Matt 24:36|of that day and hour no one knoweth: no, not the angels of heaven|De die autem illa et hora nemo scit, neque angeli cœlorum]].

paras.t: Vos autem, fratres, non estis in tenebris ignorantiæ et peccati, ut vos dies illa tanquam fur comprehendat, id est, in die illa improvise comprehendamini atque damnemini a Christo judice metuendo.
paras.en: [[5:4|But you, brethren, are not in darkness|Vos autem, fratres, non estis in tenebris]] of ignorance and sin, [[5:4|that the day should overtake you as a thief|ut vos dies illa tanquam fur comprehendat]], that is, that on that day you should be overtaken unawares and condemned by Christ, the judge to be feared.

paras.t: Occasione hujus verbi apparet quibusdam, quod in isto capitulo loquatur Apostolus potius de die particularis judicii, qua quilibet visitatur per mortem, et judicatur a Christo. Sciebat namque Apostolus diem finalis judicii multum distare : idcirco de illa non dixisset hominibus sui temporis, Vos autem in tenebris non estis, etc., quasi, si in tenebris essent, ab illa die comprehendi potuissent. Sed istud facile solvitur. Sicut enim in præcedenti capitulo dixit Apostolus de longe futuris, eis videlicet qui erunt viventes circa diem judicii, in sua persona, Nos qui vivimus, qui residui sumus, etc., ita hoc loco per præsentes, designat futuros electos, propter unitatem mystici corporis Christi.
paras.en: On the occasion of this saying it seems to some that in this chapter the Apostle is speaking rather of the day of the particular judgement, on which each one is visited by death and judged by Christ. For the Apostle knew that the day of the final judgement was far off; therefore he would not have said of it to the men of his own time, [[5:4|But you, brethren, are not in darkness|Vos autem in tenebris non estis]], etc., as though, were they in darkness, they could have been overtaken by that day. But this is easily answered. For just as in the preceding chapter the Apostle, speaking in his own person, said of those far in the future, namely those who will be alive about the day of judgement, [[1 Thess 4:14|we who are alive, who remain|Nos qui vivimus, qui residui sumus]], etc., so here by those present he means the elect who are to come, because of the unity of the mystical body of Christ.

paras.t: Verumtamen omnia jam inducta, exponi possunt de die particularis judicii. Ut sit sensus : De temporibus autem et momentis, id est, qua die et qua hora cuilibet vestrum moriturus et judicandus sit a Christo, non indigetis ut scribamus vobis. Nam ita incertum est tempus et momentum hujus judicii, sicut illius, nec spectat ad vos talia scire. Unde ait Salvator : Vigilate itaque, quia nescitis diem neque horam. Quod autem sciri de hoc potest, scitis. Ipsi enim diligenter scitis quia dies Domini, id est dies particularis judicii : quæ dicitur dies Domini, quia in ea facit Dominus cum moriente particulare judicium; sicut fur in nocte, id est improvise et subito, ita veniet : juxta illud, Qua hora non putatis, Filius hominis veniet. Et Isaias : Veniet super te malum atque calamitas, et nescies ortum eorum; veniet super te miseria repente. Quum enim dixerint homines carnales, Pax et securitas, arbitrantes diu in deliciis vivere, prout apud Lucam quidam eorum effatur : Anima, habes multa bona reposita in annos plurimos; requiesce, comede, bibe, epulare; tunc repentinus eis superveniet interitus, id est mors improvisa ac subita, sicut prædictis verbis evangelicis additur : Dixit autem illi Deus : Stulte, hac nocte animam tuam repetent a te.
paras.en: Yet everything brought forward so far can be explained of the day of the particular judgement, so that the sense is: [[5:1|But of the times and moments|De temporibus autem et momentis]], that is, on what day and at what hour each of you is to die and be judged by Christ, [[5:1|you need not, that we should write to you|non indigetis ut scribamus vobis]]. For the time and moment of this judgement are as uncertain as those of the other, and it is not for you to know such things. Hence the Saviour says: [[Matt 25:13|Watch ye therefore, because you know not the day nor the hour|Vigilate itaque, quia nescitis diem neque horam]]. But what can be known of it, you know. [[5:2|For yourselves know perfectly that the day of the Lord|Ipsi enim diligenter scitis quia dies Domini]], that is, the day of the particular judgement, which is called the day of the Lord because on it the Lord holds the particular judgement of the dying man, [[5:2|as a thief in the night|sicut fur in nocte]], that is, unexpectedly and suddenly, [[5:2|shall so come|ita veniet]]: according to that saying, [[Luke 12:40|at what hour you think not the Son of man will come|Qua hora non putatis, Filius hominis veniet]]. And Isaias: [[Is 47:11|Evil shall come upon thee, and thou shalt not know the rising thereof|Veniet super te malum atque calamitas, et nescies ortum eorum]]; [[Is 47:11|misery shall come upon thee suddenly|veniet super te miseria repente]]. [[5:3|For when they shall say|Quum enim dixerint]], that is, carnal men, [[5:3|Peace and security|Pax et securitas]], thinking to live long in delights, as one of them declares in Luke: [[Luke 12:19|Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years. Take thy rest: eat, drink, make good cheer|Anima, habes multa bona reposita in annos plurimos; requiesce, comede, bibe, epulare]]; [[5:3|then shall sudden destruction come upon them|tunc repentinus eis superveniet interitus]], that is, an unforeseen and sudden death, as is added to the words of the Gospel just quoted: [[Luke 12:20|But God said to him|Dixit autem illi Deus]]: [[Luke 12:20|Thou fool, this night do they require thy soul of thee|Stulte, hac nocte animam tuam repetent a te]].

paras.t: Denique super hæc verba, Quum dixerint, Pax et securitas, tunc repentinus eis superveniet interitus, dicit glossa : Ministri Antichristi eo occiso in diebus sequentibus gaudebunt, ducentes uxores, convivia celebrantes, et joca diversi generis exercentes, ac dicentes : Licet princeps noster mortuus sit, nos tamen pacem habemus et securitatem. Et quum talia dixerint, repentinus eis superveniet interitus. Hanc glossam reprobat quidam hoc loco, sic dicens : Illud non videtur convenienter dictum. Glossa enim præmittit quod Antichristus fulminabitur, et maxima pars sui exercitus cum ipso peribit. Non ergo est verisimile quod remanentes, erunt in tanta securitate, sed potius in timore. Et ita glossa sibimetipsi repugnare videtur. Item est contra commune dictum Sanctorum et doctorum, qui communiter asserunt omnes ad Christum convertendos, Antichristo occiso et ejus falsitate detecta.
paras.en: Further, on these words, [[5:3|For when they shall say|Quum dixerint]]: [[5:3|Peace and security|Pax et securitas]], [[5:3|then shall sudden destruction come upon them|tunc repentinus eis superveniet interitus]], the Gloss says: The ministers of Antichrist, when he has been slain, will rejoice in the days that follow, taking wives, holding banquets and practising games of every kind, and saying: Although our prince is dead, yet we have peace and security. And when they have said such things, [[5:3|sudden destruction|repentinus eis superveniet interitus]] will come upon them. A certain writer rejects this gloss in this place, saying: That does not seem fittingly said. For the Gloss states beforehand that Antichrist will be struck down by a thunderbolt, and the greater part of his army will perish with him. It is not likely, then, that those who remain will be in such security, but rather in fear. And so the Gloss seems to contradict itself. Again, it is against the common teaching of the Saints and doctors, who commonly assert that all are to be converted to Christ once Antichrist has been slain and his falsehood laid bare.

paras.t: Porro ad salvandum veritatem glossæ, et harum objectionum solutionem, hujusque dicti confutationem, primo inducenda est Scriptura canonica. Ait namque Salvator : Sicut fuit in diebus Noe, ita erit adventus Filii hominis. Sicut enim erant, inquit, in diebus Noe comedentes et bibentes, nubentesque et nuptui tradentes usque in eum diem in quo introivit in arcam Noe, et non cognoverunt donec venit diluvium et tulit omnes, ita erit adventus Filii hominis. Ex verbis his evidentissime constat, quod aliqui impii erunt in mundo, prædictis intenti operibus usque ad ipsum Christi adventum seu diem judicii. Præterea, verba Apostoli quibus dixit, Quum dixerint, Pax et securitas, Augustinus exponit de carnalibus qui non arescent præ timore et exspectatione futuri judicii. Non ergo simpliciter omnes, boni erunt.
paras.en: Now to uphold the truth of the Gloss, and to answer these objections and refute this saying, canonical Scripture must first be brought in. For the Saviour says: [[Matt 24:37|as in the days of Noe, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be|Sicut fuit in diebus Noe, ita erit adventus Filii hominis]]. [[Matt 24:38|For, as|Sicut enim erant]], he says, [[Matt 24:38|in the days before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, even till that day in which Noe entered into the ark|in diebus Noe comedentes et bibentes, nubentesque et nuptui tradentes usque in eum diem in quo introivit in arcam Noe]][[Gen 6:1||]][[Gen 7:1||]], [[Matt 24:39|and they knew not till the flood came and took them all away: so also shall the coming of the Son of man be|et non cognoverunt donec venit diluvium et tulit omnes, ita erit adventus Filii hominis]]. From these words it is most evident that some wicked men will be in the world, intent on the works just named, right up to the very coming of Christ, or the day of judgement. Besides, Augustine explains the words of the Apostle in which he said, [[5:3|For when they shall say|Quum dixerint]]: [[5:3|Peace and security|Pax et securitas]], of carnal men who are not [[Luke 21:26|withering away for fear and expectation|arescent præ timore et exspectatione]] of the judgement to come. Not all, then, will simply be good.

paras.t: Quod ergo primo arguitur, non esse verisimile quod post occisionem Antichristi, ministri ejus gaudebunt in malis, dico cum Salomone, quia quem Deus spernit, nullus corrigere potest. Ideo reprobi illi non corrigentur, visis tot signis quibus merito corrigerentur. Et hoc utique verisimile est. Legitur enim in libro Numerorum, quod postquam terra deglutivit Datan et Abiron et Core in conspectu filiorum Israel, ignis quoque devoravit ducentos quinquaginta viros fautores eorum, nihilo minus filii Israel die sequenti insurrexerunt contra Moysen et Aaron. Denique Pharao rex Ægypti quantas Dei plagas et signa vidit ac passus est? Non tamen se correxit. Gregorius quoque recitat de quibusdam, qui visis pœnis futuris, redierunt ad corpus, et tamen in vitiis permanserunt.
paras.en: As to the first argument, then, that it is not likely that after the slaying of Antichrist his ministers will rejoice in evil: I say with Solomon that [[Eccles 7:14|no man can correct whom he hath despised|quem Deus spernit, nullus corrigere potest]] [the margin gives Eccle. xii, 14; the words are at Eccles 7:14]. Hence those reprobates will not be corrected, though they have seen so many signs by which they ought rightly to be corrected. And this is certainly likely. For we read in the book of Numbers that after the earth had swallowed up Dathan and Abiron and Core in the sight of the children of Israel[[Num 16:31||]], and fire too had devoured two hundred and fifty men who supported them[[Num 16:35||]], none the less the children of Israel rose up the next day against Moses and Aaron[[Num 16:41||]]. Then too, how many plagues and signs of God did Pharao king of Egypt see and suffer[[Ex 7:1||]] [the margin gives Exod. vii–x, xii, xiv]? Yet he did not amend. Gregory also relates of some who, having seen the pains to come, returned to the body and yet remained in their vices.

paras.t: Præterea quod quidam asserit, glossam esse contra commune dictum Sanctorum et doctorum, nequaquam putandum est. Nam et glossa illa non est verbum glossatoris, videlicet Petri Lombardi, sed expositio Haymonis. Et idem dicunt Beda, Gorra, multique alii. Verum est tamen, quod Sancti affirmant totum mundum convertendum ad Christum, Antichristo occiso : quod non est intelligendum tam absolute, quod singuli convertentur, sed quia tam multi convertendi sunt, quod comparatione eorum alii erunt paucissimi. Nunc quippe sunt multi vocati et pauci electi, in terra vel in sæculo isto, tunc autem erit opposito modo.
paras.en: Again, what someone asserts, that the Gloss is against the common teaching of the Saints and doctors, is by no means to be thought. For that gloss is not the word of the glossator, namely Peter Lombard, but the exposition of Haymo. And Bede, Gorra [that is, Nicholas of Gorran], and many others say the same. It is true, however, that the Saints affirm that the whole world is to be converted to Christ once Antichrist has been slain; but this is not to be understood so absolutely as that every single person will be converted, but in this sense, that so many are to be converted that in comparison with them the others will be very few. For now, on earth or in this present age, [[Matt 20:16|many are called but few chosen|multi vocati et pauci electi]]; but then it will be the other way round.

paras.t: Cur vero Thessalonicenses non sint in tenebris, subdit Apostolus. Omnes enim vos filii lucis estis : qui ait, Ego sum lux mundi; de quo refert Evangelista : Erat lux vera quæ illuminat omnem hominem. Vel, Filii lucis, id est gratiæ et fidei. Unde ait Salvator : Dum lucem habetis, credite in lucem, ut filii lucis sitis. Et filii diei, id est temporis gratiæ seu novi Testamenti, atque virtutum. Unde ad Romanos dictum est : Nox præcessit, dies autem appropinquavit ; et Zacharias ait, Applicabuntur gentes multæ ad Dominum in die illa. Christus quoque per diem intelligi potest, sicut in Hymno cantatur : Christe, qui lux es et dies, etc. Et non estis noctis, id est temporum justæ ultionis : de quibus in Actibus Apostolorum legimus, Tempora prioris ignorantiæ despiciens Deus. Neque estis tenebrarum, id est vitiorum ac diversorum errorum : hoc est, non pertinetis ad tempora reprobationis et iræ, nec vitiis deservitis, sed estis in tempore gratiæ et statu salutis.
paras.en: Why the Thessalonians are not in darkness, the Apostle adds: [[5:5|For all you are the children of light|Omnes enim vos filii lucis estis]], that is, of him who says: [[John 8:12|I am the light of the world|Ego sum lux mundi]]; of whom the Evangelist relates: [[John 1:9|That was the true light, which enlighteneth every man|Erat lux vera quæ illuminat omnem hominem]]. Or: [[5:5|children of light|Filii lucis]], that is, of grace and faith. Hence the Saviour says: [[John 12:36|Whilst you have the light, believe in the light, that you may be the children of light|Dum lucem habetis, credite in lucem, ut filii lucis sitis]]. [[5:5|and children of the day|Et filii diei]], that is, of the time of grace, or of the New Testament, and of the virtues. Hence it is said to the Romans: [[Rom 13:12|The night is passed and the day is at hand|Nox præcessit, dies autem appropinquavit]]; and Zacharias says: [[Zach 2:11|many nations shall be joined to the Lord in that day|Applicabuntur gentes multæ ad Dominum in die illa]]. Christ too can be understood by the day, as is sung in the hymn: Christ, who art light and day, etc. [the Compline hymn *Christe qui lux es et dies*]. And you are [[5:5|not of the night|Et non estis noctis]] [Denis reads *non estis*, "you are not", where the Vulgate has *non sumus*, "we are not"], that is, of the times of just vengeance, of which we read in the Acts of the Apostles: [[Acts 17:30|God indeed having winked at the times of this ignorance|Tempora prioris ignorantiæ despiciens Deus]] [Denis reads *prioris ignorantiæ*, "of the former ignorance"]; [[5:5|nor of darkness|Neque estis tenebrarum]], that is, of vices and of divers errors: that is, you do not belong to the times of reprobation and wrath, nor are you slaves to vices, but you are in the time of grace and in the state of salvation.

paras.t: Igitur non dormiamus somno culpæ, torpendo in vitiis, sicut et ceteri ignavi, negligentes et intimorati : sed vigilemus, id est, vigili mente insistamus divinis : non enim dormientibus, sed vigilantibus provenit regnum Dei ; et sobrii simus temperantiam observando.
paras.en: [[5:6|Therefore, let us not sleep|Igitur non dormiamus]] the sleep of guilt, growing sluggish in vices, [[5:6|as others do|sicut et ceteri]] who are slothful, negligent and heedless: [[5:6|but let us watch|sed vigilemus]], that is, let us apply ourselves to divine things with a watchful mind; for the kingdom of God comes not to those who sleep but to those who watch; [[5:6|and be sober|et sobrii simus]] by keeping temperance.

paras.t: Qui enim dormiunt, jacendo in vitiis, nocte dormiunt, id est, tempore suæ internæ cæcitatis seu ignorantiæ hoc faciunt. Omnis enim peccans, est ignorans, secundum Dionysium et Aristotelem. Et qui ebrii sunt, gulose vivendo, nocte ebrii sunt, id est, in mentis caligine tales consistunt, ita ut rationis et gratiæ lumine sint privati.
paras.en: [[5:7|For they that sleep|Qui enim dormiunt]], lying in vices, [[5:7|sleep in the night|nocte dormiunt]], that is, they do this in the time of their inward blindness or ignorance. For everyone who sins is ignorant, according to Dionysius and Aristotle. [[5:7|And they that are drunk|Et qui ebrii sunt]], living gluttonously, [[5:7|are drunk in the night|nocte ebrii sunt]], that is, such men abide in darkness of mind, so that they are deprived of the light of reason and of grace.

paras.t: Nos autem qui diei sumus, id est, claritati virtutum intendimus, sobrii simus, quatenus habentes victum et vestitum, contenti simus. Unde et Sapiens orat : Tantum victui meo tribue necessaria. Induti loricam fidei et caritatis, id est sic interiora nostra armantes seu munientes fide, quantum ad intellectum, et caritate, quantum ad voluntatem, quemadmodum armatur corpus materiali lorica, et galeam spem salutis, id est, spe futuræ beatitudinis muniamus animam nostram, sicut defenditur corpus galea corporali. Nam et spe salvi facti sumus; et omnes qui sperant in Domino, non infirmantur.
paras.en: [[5:8|But let us, who are of the day|Nos autem qui diei sumus]], that is, who strive after the brightness of the virtues, [[5:8|be sober|sobrii simus]], so that, [[1 Tim 6:8|having food and wherewith to be covered|habentes victum et vestitum]], [[1 Tim 6:8|with these we are content|contenti simus]]. Hence the Wise Man too prays: [[Prov 30:8|give me only the necessaries of life|Tantum victui meo tribue necessaria]]. [[5:8|Having on the breast plate of faith and charity|Induti loricam fidei et caritatis]], that is, so arming or fortifying our inward parts with faith, as regards the intellect, and with charity, as regards the will, as the body is armed with a material breastplate; [[5:8|and, for a helmet, the hope of salvation|et galeam spem salutis]], that is, let us fortify our soul with the hope of future beatitude, as the body is defended by a bodily helmet. For indeed [[Rom 8:24|we are saved by hope|spe salvi facti sumus]]; and all who hope in the Lord are not made weak.

paras.t: Quoniam non posuit nos Deus in hoc mundo, vel in statu fidei christianæ, in iram, id est ad hoc ut pereamus, sed in acquisitionem salutis, id est ad hoc ut æternam felicitatem mereamur, per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, id est virtute et gratia ejus, qui mortuus est pro nobis salvandis ; ut sive vigilemus, id est, in hac carne vivamus, seu exterioribus sensibus et ratione utamur, sive dormiamus dormitione somni naturalis vel mortis corporalis, simul cum illo vivamus, id est, in Christo vitam gratiæ vel gloriæ habeamus.
paras.en: [[5:9|For God hath not appointed us|Quoniam non posuit nos Deus]], in this world or in the state of the Christian faith, [[5:9|unto wrath|in iram]], that is, to perish, [[5:9|but unto the purchasing of salvation|sed in acquisitionem salutis]], that is, to merit eternal happiness, [[5:9|by our Lord Jesus Christ|per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum]], that is, by his power and grace, [[5:10|Who died for us|qui mortuus est pro nobis]], to save us; [[5:10|that, whether we watch|ut sive vigilemus]], that is, live in this flesh, or use our outward senses and reason, [[5:10|or sleep|sive dormiamus]] the sleep of natural slumber or of bodily death, [[5:10|we may live together with him|simul cum illo vivamus]], that is, may have in Christ the life of grace or of glory.

paras.t: Propter quod consolamini invicem, id est, unus alium consoletur si indiget : juxta illud Ecclesiastici, Ne desis plorantibus in consolatione ; et ædificate alterutrum, id est, mutuo exemplares estote in verbis et actibus, ne quis ponat offendiculum proximo ; sicut et facitis.
paras.en: [[5:11|For which cause comfort one another|Propter quod consolamini invicem]], that is, let one comfort another if he is in need, according to that saying of Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 7:38|Be not wanting in comforting them that weep|Ne desis plorantibus in consolatione]]; [[5:11|and edify one another|et ædificate alterutrum]], that is, be examples to one another in words and deeds, lest anyone put a stumbling-block before his neighbour[[Rom 14:13||]] [the margin gives Rom. xiv without a verse; the words are at Rom 14:13]; [[5:11|as you also do|sicut et facitis]].

paras.t: Consequenter Apostolus instruit subditos. Rogamus autem vos, fratres, ut noveritis per effectum, id est, nosse vos demonstretis, eos qui laborant inter vos, et præsunt vobis in Domino, et monent vos, id est officiales superioresque vestros, qui in spiritualibus et temporalibus provident vobis, et de vestra salute solliciti sunt, ut habeatis illos abundantius solito et magis quam ceteros in caritate, diligendo eos ferventer tanquam patres spirituales ac pastores : quos tanto ferventius amare debetis, quanto majora ab eis sortimini bona. Et hunc amorem opere declarate, reverenter obediendo, atque in necessariis ministrando, propter opus illorum, id est propter exigentiam juris ex parte administrationis quam vobis impendunt. Pacem habete cum eis, nunquam murmurando, contendendo, aut rebellando. Qui enim bene præsunt presbyteri, duplici honore digni sunt. Et qui potestati resistit, Dei ordinationi resistit, damnationemque acquirit.
paras.en: Next the Apostle instructs those who are subject. [[5:12|And we beseech you, brethren, to know|Rogamus autem vos, fratres, ut noveritis]] in deed, that is, to show that you know, [[5:12|them who labour among you and are over you in the Lord and admonish you|eos qui laborant inter vos, et præsunt vobis in Domino, et monent vos]], that is, your officers and superiors, who provide for you in spiritual and temporal things and are solicitous for your salvation; [[5:13|That you esteem them more abundantly|ut habeatis illos abundantius]] than usual, and more than others, [[5:13|in charity|in caritate]], loving them fervently as spiritual fathers and shepherds: and you ought to love them the more fervently, the greater the goods you receive from them. And show this love in deed, by obeying with reverence and ministering to them in their needs, [[5:13|for their work's sake|propter opus illorum]], that is, because of what is due by right on account of the administration they spend upon you. [[5:13|Have peace with them|Pacem habete cum eis]], never murmuring, quarrelling or rebelling. For [[1 Tim 5:17|the priests that rule well|Qui enim bene præsunt presbyteri]] are [[1 Tim 5:17|worthy of double honour|duplici honore digni sunt]]. And [[Rom 13:2|he that resisteth the power resisteth the ordinance of God|qui potestati resistit, Dei ordinationi resistit]]; [[Rom 13:2|they that resist purchase to themselves damnation|damnationemque acquirit]].

paras.t: Rogamus autem vos, fratres, corripite inquietos, id est mente aut corpore instabiles, gyrovagos, curiosos, et contentiosos, consolamini pusillanimes, ne adversis frangantur, sed firmiter sperent in Deo, suscipite infirmos corde aut corpore, languorem eorum interiorem aut corporalem pro posse sanando, eosque fovendo ac supportando ; patientes estote ad omnes ; quia qui patiens est, multa gubernatur prudentia ; et in patientia consistit possessio animæ.
paras.en: [[5:14|And we beseech you, brethren, rebuke the unquiet|Rogamus autem vos, fratres, corripite inquietos]], that is, those unstable in mind or body, wanderers [Latin *gyrovagi*, the name for monks who wander from house to house], the curious and the quarrelsome; [[5:14|comfort the feeble minded|consolamini pusillanimes]], that they be not broken by adversities but hope firmly in God; [[5:14|support the weak|suscipite infirmos]] in heart or body, healing their inward or bodily sickness as far as you can, and cherishing and bearing with them; [[5:14|be patient towards all men|patientes estote ad omnes]]; for [[Prov 14:29|He that is patient, is governed with much wisdom|qui patiens est, multa gubernatur prudentia]]; and in patience lies the possession of the soul[[Luke 21:19||]] [a margin note here is unreadable; the allusion is to Luke 21:19].

paras.t: Videte ne quis malum malo alicui reddat : quoniam et alibi dictum est, Noli vinci a malo, sed vince in bono malum ; et Psalmista Si reddidi, inquiens, retribuentibus mihi mala, decidam merito ab inimicis meis inanis. Unde et Salomon in Proverbiis : Ne dicas, Quomodo fecit mihi, sic faciam ei; exspecta Dominum, et liberabit te. In Ecclesiastico quoque ait Scriptura : Relinque proximo tuo nocenti te, et tunc deprecanti tibi peccata solventur. Sed semper quod bonum est sectamini, id est, exsequamini vel imitemini, in invicem, ut unus imitetur bonum alterius, et alteri bona impendat, et in omnes extraneos sectamini bonum his modis. Virtutes igitur aliorum consideremus et imitemur, non vitia.
paras.en: [[5:15|See that none render evil for evil to any man|Videte ne quis malum malo alicui reddat]]: for it is said elsewhere too: [[Rom 12:21|Be not overcome by evil: but overcome evil by good|Noli vinci a malo, sed vince in bono malum]]; and the Psalmist: [[Ps 7:5|If I have rendered|Si reddidi]], he says, [[Ps 7:5|to them that repaid me evils, let me deservedly fall empty before my enemies|retribuentibus mihi mala, decidam merito ab inimicis meis inanis]]. Hence Solomon too in the Proverbs: [[Prov 24:29|Say not: I will do to him as he hath done to me|Ne dicas, Quomodo fecit mihi, sic faciam ei]]; [[Prov 20:22|wait for the Lord, and he will deliver thee|exspecta Dominum, et liberabit te]] [Denis joins Prov 24:29 and 20:22; no margin reference can be read here]. In Ecclesiasticus, too, Scripture says: [[Ecclus 28:2|Forgive thy neighbour if he hath hurt thee: and then shall thy sins be forgiven to thee when thou prayest|Relinque proximo tuo nocenti te, et tunc deprecanti tibi peccata solventur]]. [[5:15|But ever follow that which is good|Sed semper quod bonum est sectamini]], that is, carry it out or imitate it, [[5:15|towards each other|in invicem]], so that one imitates the good in another and does good to the other, [[5:15|and towards all men|et in omnes]] outside: follow good in these ways. Let us, then, look at the virtues of others and imitate them, not their vices.

paras.t: Semper gaudete in Domino, utputa omni tempore opportuno, tam in adversis quam prosperis. Et simili modo sine intermissione orate, nullam debitam orationis horam omittendo. In omnibus quæ accidunt vobis, et in prosperitatibus aliorum, gratias agite Deo : quemadmodum Isaias dicit, Miserationum Domini recordabor, laudem Domini super omnibus bonis quæ reddidit nobis. Hæc est enim voluntas Dei, id est, horum exsecutio placet Deo, in Christo Jesu, id est, prout Christus edocuit, et sicut ipsi in Christo hæc placuerunt, in omnibus vobis, quia vult Deus ut vos omnes ista agatis.
paras.en: [[5:16|Always rejoice|Semper gaudete]] in the Lord, that is, at every fitting time, in adversity as in prosperity. And in like manner [[5:17|pray without ceasing|sine intermissione orate]], omitting no due hour of prayer[[Luke 18:1||]]. [[5:18|In all things|In omnibus]] that befall you, and in the prosperity of others, [[5:18|give thanks|gratias agite]] to God, as Isaias says: [[Is 63:7|I will remember the tender mercies of the Lord, the praise of the Lord for all the things that the Lord hath bestowed upon us|Miserationum Domini recordabor, laudem Domini super omnibus bonis quæ reddidit nobis]]. [[5:18|For this is the will of God|Hæc est enim voluntas Dei]], that is, the doing of these things pleases God, [[5:18|in Christ Jesus|in Christo Jesu]], that is, as Christ taught, and as these things pleased him in Christ, [[5:18|concerning you all|in omnibus vobis]], because God wills that all of you do these things.

paras.t: Spiritum, id est Spiritus Sancti donum, videlicet gratiam devotionis et sancti fervoris, nolite exstinguere in vobis vel aliis, aperiendo cordis vestri januam dæmoni seu peccato mortali. Prophetias, id est expositiones Scripturarum, eloquia Prophetarum, seu revelationes quæ interdum simplicibus fiunt, nolite spernere, sed reverenter audite ac discite. Omnia autem probate, id est, universa quæ probatione digna sunt, per rationem discutite, separando pretiosum a vili. Quæ vero manifeste mala sunt atque prohibita, discussione non indigent. Quod bonum est rectæ rationis judicio, vel Scripturæ testimonio, tenete memoriter et operanter, inhærendo jugiter actibus virtuosis. Ab omni specie mala abstinete vos, id est, non solum veraciter, sed et apparenter mala vitate, ne quis scandalizetur.
paras.en: [[5:19|The spirit|Spiritum]], that is, the gift of the Holy Ghost, namely the grace of devotion and of holy fervour, [[5:19|extinguish not|nolite exstinguere]] in yourselves or in others, by opening the door of your heart to the devil or to mortal sin. [[5:20|Prophecies|Prophetias]], that is, the expositions of the Scriptures, the utterances of the Prophets, or the revelations sometimes made to simple folk, [[5:20|despise not|nolite spernere]], but hear and learn them with reverence. [[5:21|But prove all things|Omnia autem probate]], that is, examine by reason everything that deserves examining, and so [[Jer 15:19|separate the precious from the vile|separando pretiosum a vili]]. But things plainly evil and forbidden need no examining. [[5:21|That which is good|Quod bonum est]] by the judgement of right reason or by the witness of Scripture, [[5:21|hold fast|tenete]] in memory and in deed, cleaving constantly to virtuous acts. [[5:22|From all appearance of evil refrain yourselves|Ab omni specie mala abstinete vos]], that is, shun evil not only in truth but in appearance too, lest anyone be scandalized.

paras.t: Præterea orat Apostolus pro Thessalonicensibus, quatenus Deo operante, exhortationes seu jussiones præmemoratas adimpleant. Ipse autem Deus pacis dator et custos, sanctificet vos per omnia, id est, universis virtutibus mundet, ornet atque perficiat vos, ut integer, id est a corruptione vitiorum immunis, spiritus vester, et anima, quantum ad vires suas inferiores, integra a læsione peccati : incorruptio enim facit proximum esse Deo; et corpus vestrum integrum, id est inviolatum, sine querela, id est irreprehensibiliter, in adventu Domini nostri Jesu Christi, id est usque ad terminum vitæ præsentis, servetur per gratiam custodientem; vel, In adventu Christi, id est ad hoc ut in secundo Christi adventu, appareatis coram eo cum anima et corpore glorioso.
paras.en: Further, the Apostle prays for the Thessalonians, that by God's working they may fulfil the exhortations or commands given above. [[5:23|And may the God of peace himself|Ipse autem Deus pacis]], its giver and guardian, [[5:23|sanctify you in all things|sanctificet vos per omnia]], that is, cleanse, adorn and perfect you with all the virtues, [[5:23|that your whole|ut integer]], that is, free from the corruption of vices, [[5:23|spirit|spiritus vester]], [[5:23|and soul|et anima]], as regards its lower powers, whole and unharmed by sin (for [[Wis 6:20|incorruption bringeth near to God|incorruptio enim facit proximum esse Deo]]), [[5:23|and body|et corpus vestrum]] whole, that is, inviolate, [[5:23|blameless|sine querela]], that is, beyond reproach, [[5:23|in the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ|in adventu Domini nostri Jesu Christi]], that is, until the end of the present life, [[5:23|may be preserved|servetur]] by guarding grace; or: [[5:23|in the coming|In adventu]] of Christ, that is, so that at Christ's second coming you may appear before him with soul and body glorified.

paras.t: Hæc autem fidenter oro. Fidelis enim est Deus, id est verus in sermonibus suis, qui vocavit vos ad statum salutis; qui etiam faciet, id est, preces vestras exaudiet : sicut promisit de eo divinus Psaltes, Voluntatem timentium se faciet, et deprecationem eorum exaudiet. Omnis enim qui petit, accipit; et qui quærit, invenit. Quis namque invocavit eum, et despexit illum? Sed agendum est quod rursus hortatur Psalmographus : Lætetur cor quærentium Dominum; quærite Dominum et confirmamini; quærite faciem ejus semper. Qui sic invocat, procul dubio sortietur felicem effectum.
paras.en: And this I pray with confidence. For God is [[5:24|faithful|Fidelis enim est Deus]], that is, true in his words, [[5:24|who hath called you|qui vocavit vos]] to the state of salvation; [[5:24|who also will do it|qui etiam faciet]], that is, will hear your prayers, as the divine Psalmist promised of him: [[Ps 144:19|He will do the will of them that fear him: and he will hear their prayer|Voluntatem timentium se faciet, et deprecationem eorum exaudiet]]. [[Matt 7:8|For every one that asketh, receiveth: and he that seeketh, findeth|Omnis enim qui petit, accipit; et qui quærit, invenit]]. For [[Ecclus 2:12|who hath called upon him, and he despised him?|Quis namque invocavit eum, et despexit illum?]] But we must do what the Psalmist urges again: [[Ps 104:3|let the heart of them rejoice that seek the Lord|Lætetur cor quærentium Dominum]]; [[Ps 104:4|Seek ye the Lord, and be strengthened: seek his face evermore|quærite Dominum et confirmamini; quærite faciem ejus semper]] [the margin gives Ps. cv, 3–4; the words are at Ps 104:3–4]. Whoever calls on him thus will without doubt obtain a happy outcome.

paras.t: Fratres, orate pro nobis. Ecce verbum eximiæ humilitatis, quo tantus Apostolus discipulorum suorum quærit suffragium. Salutate fratres omnes vobis opportune occurrentes, in osculo sancto, non carnali aut simulato.
paras.en: [[5:25|Brethren, pray for us|Fratres, orate pro nobis]]. Here is a word of surpassing humility, by which so great an Apostle seeks the prayers of his disciples. [[5:26|Salute all the brethren|Salutate fratres omnes]] who come your way as occasion offers, [[5:26|with a holy kiss|in osculo sancto]], not a carnal or feigned one.

paras.t: Adjuro vos per Dominum, ut legatur epistola hæc omnibus sanctis fratribus, id est veraciter christianis.
paras.en: [[5:27|I charge you by the Lord that this epistle be read to all the holy brethren|Adjuro vos per Dominum, ut legatur epistola hæc omnibus sanctis fratribus]] [Latin *adjuro*, "I adjure", the word on which the question below turns], that is, to those who are truly Christians.

paras.t: Circa hoc quæri posset, quomodo adjuratio sit licita, et si liceat hominem adjurare. Et videtur quod non. Ait enim Origenes super Matthæum : Non oportet ut vir qui vult secundum Evangelium vivere, adjuret alium : si enim jurare non licet, nec adjurare. In oppositum est ipse Apostolus, adjurans hoc loco discipulos suos. Et respondendum est, secundum Thomam, quod adjurare non est alium ad jurandum inducere, sed per similitudinem juramenti a se inducti, alium ad aliquid agendum provocare. Dicitur enim adjurare, quasi ad aliquid jurare, videlicet ut aliquid fiat ab alio. Sic autem potest homo adjurare superiores suos per modum deprecationis, subditos vero per modum jussionis, quos etiam ad jurationem constringere potest propter necessariam causam. Quum vero aliquis vult ab alio quidpiam obtinere per adjurationem sine impositione necessitatis, talis adjuratio omnibus licet. Origenes autem loquitur de adjuratione, qua quis vult alium cogere ut sibimetipsi juret, quemadmodum princeps sacerdotum adjuravit Christum. Horum determinatio plenius continetur in secunda secundæ, quæstione 90.
paras.en: On this it might be asked how adjuration is lawful, and whether it is lawful to adjure a man. And it seems that it is not. For Origen says on Matthew: A man who wishes to live according to the Gospel ought not to adjure another; for if it is not lawful to swear, neither is it lawful to adjure. On the other side is the Apostle himself, adjuring his disciples in this place. And the answer, according to Thomas, is that to adjure is not to induce another to swear, but, by means of something like an oath brought in by oneself, to move another to do something. For to adjure is so called as being, as it were, to swear towards something [Latin *ad-jurare*], namely that something be done by another. In this way a man may adjure his superiors by way of entreaty, and his subjects by way of command, whom he can even bind to take an oath for a necessary cause. But when someone wishes to obtain something from another by adjuration without imposing necessity, such adjuration is lawful for all. Origen, however, is speaking of the adjuration by which someone wishes to compel another to swear to him, as the high priest adjured Christ[[Matt 26:63||]]. These things are settled more fully in the Secunda Secundæ, question 90 [that is, the second part of the second part of Thomas's *Summa Theologiae*].

paras.t: Gratia Domini nostri Jesu Christi, sine qua nullo momento esse potestis in statu salutis, sit semper vobiscum. Ipse enim ad supernaturalem finem nos condidit : ad quem perduci non possumus, nisi per supernaturalia media. Ideo nunquam de nobis præsumere, nunquam inaniter gloriari debemus, sed pietati benignissimi Creatoris indesinenter inniti, qui est super omnia Deus sublimis et benedictus. Amen.
paras.en: [[5:28|The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ|Gratia Domini nostri Jesu Christi]], without which you cannot for a single moment be in the state of salvation[[John 15:5||]], [[5:28|be|sit]] always [[5:28|with you|vobiscum]]. For he made us for a supernatural end, to which we cannot be brought except by supernatural means. Therefore we must never presume of ourselves[[Jdt 6:15||]], never glory vainly, but lean unceasingly on the loving-kindness of our most kind Creator, who is God sublime and blessed above all. [[5:28|Amen|Amen]].
